parameters.description: How far the caller cares to look, in km. Omit for the whole market.

get.description:
FB4 — the market series: kilometres of each body ASKED FOR, against kilometres actually MOVED.

 for the same reason the market board is, and more so. The list of open loads is a snapshot
anybody could assemble by watching; this is the shape of a market over time, and it is the thing nobody
else can hold, because it needs both halves — what shippers needed, and what the fleet that exists could
actually take. Giving it away is the moat, not a leak of one (user, 2026-08-30: entrepreneurs should get
that data from us, and that is how we become irreplaceable).

Nothing here identifies a load, a shipper or a driver: it is counts and kilometres, bucketed by truck
body. That is what lets an aggregate be public where the individual rows behind it are coarsened.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start, ISO. Defaults to twelve months back — the "yearly km" the series is asked for in.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end, ISO. Defaults to now.

get.description:
WHO CARRIED ON ONE LANE — the fleets, alphabetical, each with the public page it already has.

NOT @Public, and the reason is the sentence directly above that makes the series public: "nothing here
identifies a load, a shipper or a driver". Naming the carriers on a lane identifies somebody, so it
cannot ride on that justification and does not try to. It is for people signed into the market —
network staff and the companies trading in it.

It names WHOEVER THE NETWORK CONTRACTED WITH: the fleet that fielded the vehicle, or the owner-driver
who is their own. Both hold a handle and both get named — the alternative gives the incorporated an
address and the individual an anonymous residue, on a network built for informal carriers. A driver
EMPLOYED by a fleet is never named here: the load was taken from their fleet, and publishing an
employment record is the thing this network does not do.

ALPHABETICAL, NEVER BY VOLUME. The same rule as the directory: this network states what it measured
and does not publish a ranking of the people in it. The counts are there because they are measured and
a reader can check them; the ORDER makes no claim.

The fee-response curve: what share of offers at each price were actually taken.

Operator-gated, and not for drivers. It is a picture of how the whole market answers a price, and the
one legitimate use is deciding how dense the node network has to be — not telling any individual what
to charge. A driver's own view of the same machinery is their reach, on their own card.

post.description: A driver names their price for a load posted 'negotiate'. Reserves nothing — the poster's accept claims it.

get.description: The prices offered on a load. Restricted to the side that can act on them — the poster, or an operator.

post.description: The poster takes a price — and that acceptance is what claims the load.
The poster says no to one price. The load, and every other proposal on it, stay open.
A driver pulls back their own price.

Bulk freight pickup (claimed → in_transit). The driver is verified against claimedBy.

WHO THE DRIVER IS comes from the sign-in, never from the request: these four took any valid token and a driver
typed into the body, so anybody who knew which driver had claimed a load could mark it picked up, delivered or
failed in that driver's name. Network staff standing in name the driver.
Bulk freight delivery (in_transit → delivered; releases the driver's reserved capacity).

FP3 — the sender withdraws a load before the goods are taken over. The poster, the shipper (a store's order
under its store id) or staff; anybody else is told the load does not exist. Answers with the outcome, never
the freight record (it carries the buyer's hash).
FP3b — the driver stood at the door and could not hand over. The load stays on the van; the sender is told.
FP3b — the sender's claim against a delivered load: damaged, short, or not received. Answers with the claim, never the record.

get.description: FP3b — the freight claims waiting on a person, oldest first.

post.description: FP3b — decide one. Every ending carries a note the claimant is shown; an award only where a sister billed the load.

get.description: S33b — log a temperature reading for a cold-chain freight in transit (a breach flags it for the tower).
The same note as a printable page.
The whole match as a spreadsheet — every page, current filters, never just the page in front of them.

ONE DOCUMENT AS A FOLDER SOMEBODY CAN KEEP — every copy, every photograph, and a manifest.

"Can I have a copy" does not mean a link in freight. A link needs an account and this network still
running, and it points at photographs on a clock the document outlives. This is the copy that keeps
working on a laptop with no network, which is the only kind worth calling an export.
The same, for everything matching a filter — the shape an audit asks for: "everything you moved in 2026".
The webhook signing secret, for setting the far end up. Shown to the owner, nobody else.

post.description:
Write a real file and report what happened.

Not a ping: the failures people hit are credentials that read but cannot write, and a bucket that
exists with a prefix that is denied. Only a real PUT finds those, and finding them now rather than
a year later — when the document has gone — is the entire point of the button.

get.description: What has been delivered and what is still owed — so a destination that stopped working is visible.

post.description:
IS THIS THE DOCUMENT YOU ISSUED? — public, and deliberately so.

The people who most need this answer have no account here and never will: an insurer weighing a
claim, a forwarder, a magistrate, the other side's lawyer. A fingerprint cannot be guessed or
reversed, so whoever is asking already holds the document; there is nothing here to probe at. It
answers about the fingerprint alone — never the note, never the parties, never the route — and it
keeps answering for good, long after the document itself has been deleted at the end of its window.

get.description: One document: what it is, and every copy of it with its fingerprint. The notes stay behind the copies.
One copy, exactly as it was frozen. `0` is the newest.
The same copy as the printable page a party files — rendered from what was frozen, never from the load.
F3 — a cooperative's own consolidation lots (owner-scoped; an operator must name the owner).

post.description:
F3 — record a member deposit into a lot (auto-posts the freight the moment the lot fills). Owner-scoped
 to the lot's owner (403 for another shop).
F3 — sweep: post every full/aged lot to the marketplace (operator-triggered; a cron would call this).

A driver declares a route A→B → the platform suggests the loads sitting on the way.

A ROUTE IS A PLAN, NOT A POSITION. This used to write A into the live map as where the driver was —
stamped with a fresh "located at" time, so it read as a reading rather than a guess — while the driver
could be planning tomorrow's run from home. It did worse than guess: it OVERWROTE the real fix the
phone reports while on shift (see /locate), and it published DriverMoved, which is what nudges a
driver about a load they are "about to drive past" — past a place they were never at. Where the driver
is comes only from the phone. With location refused, the map shows no position rather than a made-up one.
Driver GPS heartbeat — updates the vehicle's position on the live fleet map.

get.description:
Fleet-manager dashboard: vehicle/driver/session counts, working hours, live positions + cargo.
A fleet manager sees ONLY their own fleet (actor.tenant); the ?manager= scope and the omit-for-all
view are operator-only. Before S3 anyone could pass ?manager= to read a competitor's fleet.

A driver's JOBS + EARNINGS register (R5): the dedicated-freight hauls they claimed, server-side searched /
 filtered / sorted / paginated → { items, total }. Each row carries the driver's agreed earning (lockedPrice)
 and whether it has been paid. Owner-scoped (403 for another driver).

Running totals for the current filter, and — separately — what has actually been PAID.

They are two different questions and the screen used to answer only one of them under the other's
name. `earned`/`paid`/`unpaid` come from the jobs themselves, where "paid" means the network booked
what it owes at the moment of delivery. `settlement` comes from the payouts, where paid means a rail
confirmed money leaving. Until settlement existed there was nothing to tell apart; now there is, and
conflating them would tell somebody they have their money when it is still in the sister's account.
Export the whole matching set (every page, current filters) as CSV — the driver's OWN earnings export. Owner-scoped.

post.description:
Driver accepts a suggestion → reserves the load + its weight against the vehicle's capacity.

AN OFFER IS MADE TO ONE DRIVER, and is theirs to take or leave — from their own sign-in, or network staff
standing in. Its id was all these two took: any account could accept a load onto somebody's van, or throw
somebody's offers away.
Driver declines a suggestion.

Decline an offer straight from the notification's "Not now", using the one-shot capability that rode in
the push. PUBLIC by necessity and safe by construction: the service worker handling that tap has no
session, and the alternative — handing a background script the driver's token — trades a one-word
problem for their whole identity. The token is unguessable, bound to a single offer, single-use, and
dead when the offer lapses (see mintDeclineToken). It carries no authority to claim anything.

Enroll (or return) the consumer for an OTP-verified phone; optionally set the PIN in the same step.
Requires the phone to have been verified via `sbg/auth/phone/verify` first — the OTP is the identity
proof; enroll consumes it (one verification → one enrolment), so a stale verification can't be reused.

A code to an email address, to CONFIRM it as a recovery address. Echoed in the answer only in a sandbox — anywhere
else, handing it to whoever asked would let anyone confirm anyone's inbox.

A code to the address ON an account — to get back in, or to undo a number change. Answers the same whether or
not any account uses that address: this door tells a stranger nothing about who is registered.

UNDO A NUMBER CHANGE — within 24 hours, with the OLD number and the PIN as it was, or with a code to the
account's email. The account goes back to the old number, every phone is signed out and the PIN is locked:
whoever moved it knew the PIN.

GET BACK IN WHEN THE NUMBER IS GONE AND THE PIN FORGOTTEN: the inbox, the national ID where the account has one,
a new number confirmed by code, a new PIN. It can be undone for 24 hours like any number change.

THIS DEVICE, CONFIRMED BY THE CODE — for somebody who has an account and a PIN and is on a device their PIN has
never been used on. `auth/phone/request` sent the code and `auth/phone/verify` checked it; this hands the device
its key and spends the confirmation. Nothing about the account changes: the PIN is the one they had.

Reopen the app: phone + PIN, no code — ON A DEVICE THE CODE WAS ONCE TYPED ON (`device`). Anywhere else the
answer is DEVICE_NOT_KNOWN and the PIN is not looked at. Locks after repeated wrong PINs — then the code again.
Set or change the signed-in person's PIN.

Change your PIN — proven with the CURRENT PIN, not with a session (a phone left unlocked is not proof of who
holds it). A wrong current PIN counts toward the lockout. Other sessions end; this one gets a fresh sign-in.

get.description: The signed-in person + every role they hold (the role switcher reads this) + their self profile.

patch.description: Set the signed-in person's own display name and/or avatar (S29). Returns the updated self-view.

post.description: "Act as" a held role → an actor token carrying that role's scopes + tenant.

get.description:
The receiver/sender home: every parcel this person is a party to (sent + received). Theirs is what belongs to
their ACCOUNT, and — retroactively (O4) — what is addressed to the number they sign in with and belongs to no
account yet; never what belonged to whoever had that number before. PII-free authenticated twins; the counterpart
stays hashed. S32d
also returns `freights` — any order of theirs that was too big for the parcel network and diverted to
dedicated freight, so a diverted order never vanishes from the buyer's home.

post.description:
PG1 — parcel genesis from the sender's own phone: the IDENTICAL mint the vendor console gets (derived
size + cargo gate, locked price, shipment DID + twin + planned journey + printable label at creation).
Cash at the counter: the price locks NOW and the shop collects it at drop-off — so the label (the
sender's drop-off credential) issues immediately. The sender's identity comes from the TOKEN, never
the body. A P4+ load is REFUSED here (not diverted like a vendor's): the freight lane bills a shipper
at claim through the vendor prepaid rail, and a person has no billing rail yet — a silent divert would
be un-priced, un-consented free freight (the driver still gets paid). Refusing keeps the money
invariant; the Send UI explains and points at a PUDO shop.

get.description: One parcel the caller is a party to — the authenticated twin + status timeline (404 to a non-party).

post.description: The receiver attaches their own delivered-state photo (proof of what they received) — S23.

The receiver answers the final notice — the four things a person can do about a closed window.

On their OWN parcel only, and 404 otherwise: this is the one screen in the network where somebody
can give up a claim to goods, so it must not be possible to do it to somebody else's.

Returns their twin rather than a bare acknowledgement, because three of the four choices change what
the app should be showing them and a screen that has to guess will guess wrong.

The receiver names somebody to collect for them.

The code comes BACK to the receiver, which is the point: they are the one who has to pass it on, and
a code the network delivered straight to the neighbour would be the network deciding who a person
trusts. Their own code keeps working alongside it, and the shop still learns neither.

The receiver rates the STORE they bought from — stars and tags, on a parcel we actually carried.

That last part is the whole point: a public review site cannot tell a real customer from a paid one,
and we can, because we moved the parcel. Verified beats volume. One verdict per shipment, so nobody
can stack a merchant either way, and only after delivery — an opinion about a parcel that has not
arrived is an opinion about waiting, which the measured half already reports better.
The receiver files a delivery dispute (reason + photo) → routed to the vendor / sender + control tower.
Create (or return) an invite for a contact → a token the app turns into a shareable /send/ link (S24).

get.description: The inviter's sent invites + how many turned into joins (the growth credit) — PII-free.
The invite landing check — validates the token without exposing the inviter or the invitee.

Who is signed in, as the menu needs them: name, photo, address, when the PIN last changed, and the
handle of the role they are acting as, where that role has one.

Note what it does NOT do: invent a handle. `handleOf` looks up the acting DID and answers nothing for
a fleet driver, who has no public page by design — the menu simply omits the row.

patch.description: Set the person's own name, photo or address. Each field independent; an empty address clears it.

post.description:
Change the PIN, proven with the current one.

KEYED TO THE TOKEN, never to a phone number in the body — the whole account is, and this is the field
where it matters most. A route that took a phone would change the PIN of whatever account that number
named, so one hostile body would be enough, and checking afterwards is no check at all because the
credential has already moved.

The wrong-PIN counter is the door's, so a guess here costs the same as a guess at sign-in: an open
session is not proof of who is holding the phone.

Every other session that PIN opened is ended — including, necessarily, the one that made this call,
because the token carries the person as its revocation key. So the app that calls this signs the
person back in rather than carrying on; the response deliberately hands back no token, since the
consumer one the spine mints is not the role token the caller came in with.

THE PHONES AND BROWSERS MY PIN WORKS ON — how many, when each was confirmed by a code and last used, and which
one this is. A POST although it only reads: the browser's device keys come in the body, never in an address,
which is written to logs. Keyed to the token, like everything here.

FORGET EVERY OTHER PHONE AND BROWSER — the PIN again. Each of them needs the code to the number before the PIN
works there again, and every session is ended, this one included: the app signs the person back in here.

FORGET THIS ONE, AND SIGN OUT — for a computer that is not theirs. From then on the PIN does not work on it
until a code to the number is typed there again.

Set or replace the recovery email — the PIN again (an open session is not proof of who holds the phone), and
the code sent to the NEW address. The address it replaces is told, because whoever swaps the email is one
step from owning the account.

MOVE THIS ACCOUNT TO ANOTHER PHONE NUMBER — by the person themselves, signed in. The PIN again, and a code
already confirmed on the new number (auth/phone/request + verify). No staff and no ID: the PIN already opens
the whole account. Keyed to the token, never to a number in the body.

Every session ends, this one included; they sign in again with the new number and the same PIN. It can be
undone for 24 hours, and the old number is held for them until then.

BLOCK MY OLD NUMBER — the user, 2026-10-08: "the user blocks their own old phone number in the account."

For a week after a move, what is sent to the old number still reaches the account. When the people and the stores
that send to them have the new one, the holder lets the old number go here, rather than waiting for the week to
end. The PIN again; keyed to the token, never to a number in the body. Refused while the move can still be undone:
the old number is where the account would go back to. Answers with the account as it now stands.
What became of a request. The reference goes in the body: it is not a thing to leave in an address.
"That was not me." Ends every request waiting against the account of whoever is signed in.
The first member of staff: who is asking was checked, and this is what was checked. Moves nothing.
The second, different member of staff approves — and the account moves.
One of the three photographs. Taken again, it replaces the one before.
Still disputed: a day to come in. Answers with the ticket.
"The number on my record is not mine — this one is." Ends a dispute over their ID at once, or a hold it left.
The number read on a card: only whether it is the disputed one comes back, and is kept.
The first member of staff says whose it is — from the photographs, or after an appointment. Changes nothing.
The second, different member of staff approves — and it is done.

REPORT ONE OF THEM. What is reported is worked out HERE, from what this reader was shown: the company from their
own record, the paper from the licence or policy they name on that company's record. Never a company or a
document id from the request — a report could otherwise be aimed at any company's paper.

get.description: What a reporter, or the company, attached — with the fingerprint it arrived under and whether the bytes still match it.

post.description: Upload one downscaled image (+ optional thumbnail). The owner is the authenticated caller.

get.description: The caller's own media — the source for the media library (S27). PII-free projection.
Stream one image's bytes (or its thumbnail via ?variant=thumb). Owner-or-operator only.

delete.description: Remove one of your own asset images early (vehicle/trailer only — evidence bins stay locked).

get.description:
Every option of one vocabulary, with the picture where one is curated.

The whole topic in one request, deliberately: a picker needs all of it to render, and the "not sure"
sheet shows every option side by side. One request per option would make that sheet a waterfall on the
exact connection least able to afford it.

One option's illustration bytes.

PUBLIC and immutable-cacheable: the URL carries the blob id as `?v=`, so a replaced picture is a new URL
and the old one can be cached hard without ever going stale. nosniff because these bytes are served to
a browser — the upload path already refuses anything whose magic number is not a real raster image.

put.description: Set or replace one option's illustration. Operator-only — see the class note.

delete.description: Remove one option's illustration. The option stays; its sheet falls back to text alone.

get.description: The `applicationServerKey` the browser needs to build a PushSubscription. Public, not a secret.

post.description: Enrol this device (the browser's PushSubscription) for the authenticated owner.

delete.description: Drop this device (the browser unsubscribed, or the user turned notifications off).

post.description: Send a test push to every device the owner has enrolled — the "it works" confirmation after opt-in.

get.description: The caller's notification inbox (newest first) + the unread count — the in-app notification centre (N2).

post.description: Mark one of the caller's notifications read. Ownership-guarded in the service.
Mark all of the caller's notifications read (clears the bell badge).

What would this cost to ship? Creates nothing — no parcel, no account, no reservation.

The one call the "calculate your shipping fee" button makes. A key is optional: send one in
`X-SBG-Key` and the limit becomes yours rather than your IP's, and a server-side key also returns the
costed breakdown.

Turn a price into a shipment. Needs a SECRET key: a credential that ships things must never sit in a
page. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header and the same name is spent at most once, however many times a
flaky network makes you ask.

A TEST key runs every check and creates nothing — see ShippingApiService.mint.

get.description:
Where the network can deliver: every country it operates in and the areas inside it that have a
collection point somebody can actually stand at. What a destination picker is built from.

Where is my shipment? The state of one you created, read back by the key that created it.

The price comes off the parcel, not from a fresh quote: re-pricing a sold shipment would have this
endpoint disagree with the merchant's own invoice. Somebody else's shipment answers NOT FOUND rather
than FORBIDDEN — "you may not see this" tells a stranger the id is real.

The collection code is NOT here. It arrives on the `ready_for_pickup` callback, at the moment it is
useful and to an endpoint the store registered; on a pollable read it would sit in every log file that
ever recorded a response body.

post.description:
Call it off, while it still can be.

A secret key, for the reason minting needs one: a credential that can undo a shipment must never sit
in a page. The window is the network's own — Created, At_PUDO or At_MDP — and once somebody is
carrying it, calling it off is a conversation rather than an API call.

THERE IS NO AMEND, deliberately. Moving a parcel's destination or changing its size changes what it
costs, and an "edit" that quietly re-prices something a buyer already paid for is the worst possible
version of this call. Cancel and create the replacement, so the new price is seen and agreed.
Ask about a load — or (CV5) talk about a parcel waiting at a shop. Either returns to the thread already open.

get.description: Reported messages, newest first — the operator's review list (CV3 gives it a screen).
CV3 — the conversations this fleet's drivers chose to share with it. Read-only.
CV3 — the reports of chosen messages that parties shared — the operator's side of a dispute.
CV4 — the operator plays a voice message a party chose to include in a shared report.

post.description: CV4 — send a voice message.

get.description: CV4 — play a voice message: the thread's readers only. Never cached, never sniffed as something else.

post.description: CV3 — the driver shares this conversation with their fleet manager, or stops sharing it.
CV3 — a party shares a report of the messages they choose. The other side is told in the thread.
CV2 — the driver names a price, through the load's own negotiation.
CV2 — the poster accepts a price in the thread. Accepting claims the load for that driver.
CV2 — write down how a load the network does not pay will be settled.
CV2 — the other party agrees to a written-down settlement.

get.description: The businesses this person is in, and the ones they are invited to.

post.description: Open one business: a session that acts as it, for a person who is in it.

delete.description: Take somebody out — or, on your own row, leave. A viewer may leave too: that is not changing the business.

post.description: Ask SeeBuyGet to check the business, once its papers are on record.
Archive, or bring back. Never deleted: what was sent for them keeps naming them.
Approve — the first of two, or the second. Never twice by the same member of staff.
Paid, or back to open — confirmed by a party, with their reference.
The payer agrees to the figure.
Attach the proforma invoice — either party, kept as handed over.
The run's price is the carrier's published rate, agreed by booking; the shipper may state what was invoiced.
A code for the shipper's business to link the contract with. Shown once; a new one replaces the last.

get.description: The orders this fleet must carry, by the day they must arrive.

post.description:
P1b — a sheet of orders for one contract. Sent first as a CHECK (`dryRun`, the default): every line judged, nothing
created. Sent again with `dryRun: false`, the good lines become orders and the rest are left out and said why.

get.description: The sheet to hand a shipper: the columns by the names the import reads, and one line showing each form.

post.description: The office puts an uploaded order's delivery address on the map, so it can be planned.
The office withdraws an order it uploaded itself. One the shipper placed is the shipper's to withdraw.

Split an order into loads — for one that is more than a vehicle carries. The office's act, on an order that is
still its own to plan; the shipper is told. The loads add up to the order.
Put an order back together, while every load of it is still an order: none on a truck, none handed on.

get.description: The plan accepted for a day, as accepted, and what has changed under it since.

post.description: Accept the plan for a day. Worked out again here from the same asks, kept, and written onto its orders.
P3b — send the next trip to every truck in TODAY's accepted plan that is ready for one.

get.description:
THE FLEET'S OWN CLOCK — which time zone its plans, its "today" and its deliveries are read on, where that comes
from, and what time it is there now. The office's alone to read, and to set.
P5 — can this server reach the adviser at all? The screen asks before it offers one.

post.description:
P5 — say something to the adviser about a day's plan: a question, or what to change. It answers with words and
with a PROPOSAL the solver worked out; nothing is accepted and nothing is sent to a driver by asking.
Link a contract with the fleet's code. An owner's act: it commits the business to the fleet as its carrier.

get.description: A driver's own coming days. Theirs, their fleet office's and the network's to read — as their hours are.
How the fleet's vehicles were used, from a day to a day: its office's and staff's to read.

post.description: Where a vehicle or a driver works from.
The office's reading: at a service, or a new meter (which may be lower than the last).
What was done to it, and when: a service, a repair, tyres, an inspection — with its job card.

get.description: A service's job card, to the vehicle's owner — asked of the service, never of the photo, so it stays the vehicle's.

post.description: A breakdown the office heard of by telephone — or an owner-driver's own vehicle.
How it ended: back on the road, or into the workshop — with what was done.

get.description: A breakdown's photograph, to the vehicle's owner — asked of the breakdown, never of the photo.
The broken-down vehicles of the driver's own fleet with loads still to take over — for the driver coming for them.

post.description: Taking a broken-down vehicle's loads over, at the vehicle, with the pass of the driver handing them over.

get.description: Who of the fleet could take a breakdown's loads: out in another vehicle on the road now, and the room each has.

post.description: The office moves a breakdown's loads to a driver of the fleet out in another vehicle.

get.description: A fleet's vehicles broken down now: its office's and staff's to read.

post.description: A defect reported by the driver, on the vehicle named or the one they are out in.
A defect reported by the office (or an owner-driver for their own vehicle) — it says whether it is safe to drive.
The office's word on a defect: fixed, or safe to drive as it is.

get.description: A defect's photograph, to the vehicle's owner — asked of the defect, never of the photo, so it stays the vehicle's.
A fleet's own rules for its vehicles' upkeep: its office's and staff's to read and set.

post.description: Name a fleet to hand overflow to. The answer carries the code to pass on — shown this once.

May this partner pass your orders on to a fleet of its own. The offering fleet's switch, off until it is turned
on. Turned off, an order already passed on stays with whoever carries it; offers still open are taken back.
A partner that took orders offers them on to its own partners — where the fleet they came from allows it.
A partner takes an order it was offered.
A partner leaves an order it was offered.
A partner gives back an order it had taken, before it is on a truck — with a reason.
Release orders to the open board: any checked carrier may take them.
Take an order back off the open board, while nobody has taken it.

Ask the routing server now. The two places are a fleet's depot and a point a little way off it: places a plan
would really ask about, on whatever map the operator's server holds.
What this link is, before the file is taken: what it opens and until when — or which way it stopped.
The file: the note, every copy of it and its photographs, as the party the link was made for may read them.

get.description: The links made for the caller on one of their documents.

post.description: Make a link to pass on. The address in the answer is shown this once: the key is not kept.
Cancel one: it opens nothing from now on.

get.description: Every problem reported, newest first. Staff read; nothing here is decided by them.
The report on one parcel, for whoever it is for.
The file: the report to read or print, the same facts for a machine, and the photographs.

post.description: The links the caller made on this report.
Make a link to pass on. The address in the answer is shown this once: the key is not kept.
Cancel one: it opens nothing from now on.
What this link is, before the file is taken — or which way it stopped.
The file, for whoever holds a link that still opens.

get.description: Triple-entry journal + chain verification (SSE-082).

info.title: SeeBuyGet API
info.description: SeeBuyGet — see, buy, get. The API behind the SeeBuyGet network: the PUDO pick-up/drop-off agents, drivers, fleets and MDP sort hubs that move a parcel, plus the seebuyget.com consumer web (storefront, checkout, tracking). Authenticate with the actor token minted at login.

providerRef.description: The payment's own reference on the statement or provider receipt — the thing an auditor can look up.

amount.description: What actually arrived. The rail is the authority on this, never what was asked for.

provider.description: Which rail carried it, if it was not a plain bank transfer.

fee.description: What the provider took to move it. Our expense — never netted off the payer’s credit.

providerRef.description: The payment's own reference on the statement or provider receipt — the thing an auditor can look up.

amount.description: What actually arrived. The rail is the authority on this, never what was asked for.

provider.description: Which rail carried it, if it was not a plain bank transfer.

fee.description: What the provider took to move it. Our expense — never netted off the payer’s credit.

reference.description: Pretend the payer quoted this instead — an empty string means they quoted none. SANDBOX ONLY.

payerDid.description: The shop’s DID or the store’s id — chosen from a list, never typed.

by.description: The person deciding. Recorded on the payment, because this is a judgement.

entityId.description: The sister collecting it — rule 1, collection follows the payer. Its books are where this posts.

payerName.description:
WHO IS PAYING, in the words somebody would use out loud — "Mama Sarah Shop", not a DID.

Stamped when the request is opened, because that is the only moment the payer is resolved and because
a name that is re-read later is a name that can change under a record it is describing. This console
has a standing rule about it: never an id where a name belongs. A row that says
`did:glos:ab6ed968206e6…` is a row nobody can act on without a second lookup.

amount.description:
What was ASKED for. Never what moved: `confirmedAmount` is what moved, and where the two differ the
pair is the whole story. Kept even after confirmation for that reason.

reference.description:
OUR reference, the thing the payer quotes when they pay — a paybill account number, an airtime
top-up memo, the reference line on a transfer. Short and human-typeable on purpose: it is read off a
phone screen and typed into another phone, often by somebody standing at a counter.

provider.description: Which rail this was opened against. A sister's paybill is not the same as its card acquirer.

instructions.description:
The words the payer is shown. The RAIL's words, kept with the intent so the screen cannot drift
 from what the provider actually needs — the same reason the CL5 consent notice travels with the gate.

pushed.description:
WHETHER A PROMPT WENT TO A PHONE, or whether this payer has to go and pay the long way.

Recorded rather than derived from "did we have a number", because the two differ exactly when it
matters: a number was given, the push was refused by Safaricom, and the shop must be shown the
paybill instead of a promise. Absent on every record opened before STK existed, which reads as false.

railRef.description:
The provider's handle for the request behind that prompt — a CheckoutRequestID. What you quote when
 a shopkeeper says no prompt ever came.

providerRef.description:
The provider's own reference for the money that arrived. The thing you quote when somebody says
 they paid and we say we never saw it.

confirmedAmount.description: What actually arrived, in the currency above. Present only once confirmed.

fee.description:
What the rail took to move it. An expense of ours, never netted off the payer's credit — see
 the money model: "credit the GROSS at top-up, never net-credit".

entryId.description: The journal entry that created the money. Present ONLY once confirmed — before that nothing moved.

reversalEntryId.description: …and the entry that took it back, if the payment was later recalled.

consolidationSlots.description: Labels (e.g. "Green-3") the agent designates as consolidation/bundle slots for small parcels.

country.description: The country the shop stands in (ISO-3166 alpha-2). Omitted = this deployment's home country.

The country this shop stands in (ISO-3166 alpha-2). It decides which sister contracts it, and a
 journey that leaves it crosses a border. Absent on every pre-slice record, which reads as this
 deployment's home country — read it through AgentService.countryOf, never off the field.

entityId.description:
The sister company this shop is contracted to — it buys the shop's handling and owes it the fee.
 A shop sits in exactly one country, so this is unambiguous. Absent on pre-entity records; read it
 through AgentService.entityIdOf().

signupNudgedFor.description:
What the last onboarding nudge was ABOUT — the missing set it named, e.g. "id,licence,photos" or
 "rejected" or "unfunded". Said once per distinct gap: progress starts a new clock, and an ignored
 nudge is never repeated. Follows CredentialReminderService's stamp-against-the-state rule.

reason.description:
Required when refusing: the applicant is SHOWN this, and a refusal they cannot act on leaves them
 exactly where a silent one did. Validated in the service, where the approve flag is known.

message.description: Why they are asking. The motivation is the evidence a switch-on decision is made on.

reason.description: Required to decline: a refusal is kept with its reason.

origin.description: Permitted where this country is the ORIGIN of the load.

destination.description: Permitted where this country is the DESTINATION.

termGains.description: CL1 — the terms this proposal would switch on, as words a second person can read.

incoterms.description: CL1 — the full sets as proposed, applied verbatim on approval.

gains.description: What the country would be able to do that it cannot now — the reason this needs a second person.

reason.description: Why it was declined. Required there, because a refusal nobody can read cannot be argued with.

mine.description: On a listing, for whoever reads it: THEY proposed this one, so they are not the one to approve it. Never stored.

merchantOfRecord.description: May we contract with, and charge, a consumer here? Without it there is no redeemable quote.

holdFloat.description: May a shop's prepaid float sit with us? Holding other people's money is the regulated part.

cashOnDelivery.description: May cash we are answerable for pass across a counter?

claims.description:
Is there a provision that can actually pay an award? Where there is not, cover is ZERO by
 construction — never "unset", and never a limit nobody can honour.

tax.description: Do we collect and remit here?

payouts.description: May money leave to a local supplier, in local currency?

takeIn.description: May a shop here take goods into custody at all — and under whose promise? See `TakeInPromise`.

fieldEvidence.description:
CL5 — MAY WE HOLD A PHOTOGRAPH OF AN OFFICIAL DOCUMENT HERE?

The only capability NO level grants. Every other one arrives with the level that earns it; this one
arrives only when somebody switches it on for a named country, which under CA2 is a proposal by one
person and an approval by a different one.

The user settled the question this slice was blocked on: "cl5 is by default off because it's correct
that we cant just hold photographs of official documents." Quite so. A photograph of a customs entry
or an inspection notice may itself be a controlled record in the jurisdiction it came from, and being
ESTABLISHED in a country is no answer to that — it is a different question, asked of a lawyer, about
that country. So the default is off at established too, and nothing but a deliberate act turns it on.

THIS IS THE FIRST OF TWO GATES. The second belongs to the person holding the camera, and neither
substitutes for the other — see FieldObservationService.

expiredAt.description: The last day it was good for (YYYY-MM-DD).

hasEntity.description: True where a transacting sister actually exists. Established cannot be claimed without one.

lapses.description: CA5 — capabilities switched off because a licence or policy lapsed, each naming the paper that did it.

recorded.description: Whether this country was ever recorded, or is simply unknown — which resolves to `observed`.

incoterms.description: CL1 — the trade terms allowed here, per direction. Always present, empty where none are switched on.

approvedBy.description: CA2 — the second person who approved the change that raised this country.

note.description: Why. A country’s standing is a decision, and a decision with no reason cannot be reviewed.

hours.description: Opening hours as the post states them ("06:00–22:00", "24 hours").

from.description: The country the vehicle comes FROM (and is registered in, for cabotage).

permits.description: Transit permits a vehicle needs to cross (named as the authority names them).

regionalInsurance.description: Regional insurance it must carry — e.g. the COMESA Yellow Card.

cabotage.description: May a vehicle from `from` carry a load that starts and ends inside `to`?

freeAbove.description:
Top up this much or more and it costs nothing. In the sister's own currency, like every other figure
it holds. Zero would make the fee unreachable, which is a confusing way to write "no fee" — leave the
whole rule off instead.

amount.description: The flat charge below that threshold, in the same currency.

country.description: ISO-3166 — a registered address may sit in another country (a branch of a foreign company).

sharePct.description: Percentage held, above zero and at most a hundred; all owners together never exceed a hundred.

expiresAt.description: YYYY-MM-DD. A licence with no expiry is not accepted: the watch cannot guard what it cannot date.

jurisdiction.description:
ISO-3166-alpha-2. Required for a sister (it is what makes it the merchant of record there);
 absent on the group, whose country of incorporation nothing in the system depends on.

currency.description:
The currency this entity settles in, derived from its jurisdiction. A group has none: it holds
 no custody account, so there is no balance for a currency to describe.

feePct.description:
The margin this sister charges on top of provider costs, as a fraction (0.02 = 2%). A knob each
market turns for itself rather than a constant of the network — Nairobi and Amsterdam do not have to
price alike. Absent means "the network default"; read it through EntityService.feePctOf(), never
off the record, so a sister created before the knob existed still answers.

SUPERSEDED BY `rates` and kept as its input: a sister that only ever set this one number is read as
having set that number as its MARGIN. It is not migrated on write, because a value that rewrites
itself the first time anything reads it makes the record's history unreadable.

rates.description:
What this sister charges, in the three layers a business actually decides separately.

One blended percentage cannot answer "are we earning because the market is good, or because we are
carrying risk nobody is paying us for?" — and that is the question the knobs exist to answer.

ratesByLane.description:
Per-lane overrides, keyed by the CALLER'S vocabulary (today a CargoLane: pudo | mdp | dedicated).

A plain string map because the lane taxonomy belongs to the pudo module and this is foundation — the
books must not learn what a parcel is in order to hold a number. The caller validates the key; this
only ever validates the rates.

Absent lane → the sister's own `rates` → `feePct` as a margin → the network default. Four steps, each
one a real state some sister is in.

taxRegistration.description:
The registration this sister collects tax under — its VAT/TIN/GST number in its own country.

Not the same thing as being incorporated there, which `jurisdiction` already says: a company can be
registered to trade and not registered to collect, and below a turnover threshold that is the normal
state. So this is separate, and absent means "not registered to collect" rather than "unknown".

tax.description:
What this sister charges in tax on everything it sells. Absent means none — the network default, and
the state every sister is in until an operator deliberately says otherwise.

topUpFee.description:
What a shop or store pays this sister to put money in. Absent means nothing — see TopUpFeeRule for
why the cost is recovered here rather than folded into a parcel price. Read it through
`EntityService.topUpFeeFor()`, never off the record, so a sister created before the knob still answers.

amounts.description:
What a parcel costs and what each step pays, where this company has set its own figure. A key that is absent
stands at what every company starts from. Read it through `EntityService.amountsFor()`, never off the record.

taxByLane.description:
Per-lane tax overrides, keyed by the caller's vocabulary exactly as `ratesByLane` is.

Here for a reason narrower than it looks: tax rates vary by what is SUPPLIED, and lane is the only
supply-type axis this system has. A jurisdiction that zero-rates one kind of transport and standard-
rates another can express that; everyone else sets one rate and never touches this.

insurance.description:
What this sister covers when it breaks something, and what it charges to cover more.

Absent means the network default — no free cover and no premium charged, which is where every sister
starts. Read it through EntityService.insuranceFor(), never off the record.

carrierPapers.description:
Which of a CARRIER'S own papers this sister will not trade without. Absent enforces nothing, which
is where every sister starts. Read it through EntityService.carrierPapersFor(), never off the record.

parentEntityId.description: Sisters point at the group they belong to.

status.description:
CA3 — a company created from the console starts as a DRAFT: recorded, documented, and able to do nothing at all
until its record is ready and two people approve the country up to it. Absent means active (the seeds).

record.description: CA3 — the legal record: form, registration, representatives, owners, tax numbers, bank, licences, insurance.

relatesTo.description: Which licence, policy (its number) or obligation (its key) this paper is for.

mode.description:
How the goods arrived — sea, air, road, rail. A LABEL: no airline, no waybill, no schedule.

It has to be on the DTO and not only on the service, which is what the drive caught: validation
whitelists, so a field the DTO does not declare is stripped in silence and an air consignment was
recorded as sea. The service accepted it and nothing errored anywhere.

importerEntityId.description: Whose goods. A company administrator may only name their own; staff must name one.

destPort.description: Where it CLEARS. A saved place of kind 'clearance' supplies this on a screen; staff may type it.

dischargePort.description: Where the vessel put it down, when that is somewhere else. A label off a bill of lading.

carrierRef.description: The carrier's own reference. Recorded, and read by nothing yet — the carrier seam is not wired.

lastCargoes.description: What it last held, most recent first. The trade usually wants three. Their words.

certificateDocumentId.description: One of the importer's own documents — the cleaning certificate. Never a file uploaded into here.

unNumber.description: 'UN1202'. Carried as the importer wrote it; we validate the shape and never the choice.

key.description: A slug the agent chooses, unique within this consignment — what `supply` and `accept` name.

label.description: The agent's own words: "Investment licence", "Ministry of Agriculture permit".

copies.description: How many physical copies the counter wants. Some of the user's papers were wanted in ten.

documentId.description: What the importer attached. One of THEIR OWN documents, never a file uploaded into this list.

at.description: When it happened, as the party recording it says. Their date, not ours: we were not there.

releasedAt.description: When it ended, once somebody records that it has. Absent while a container is still held.

accounts.description: Every account given, oldest first, including the one that recorded it.

code.description: IMP-001. Also the `relatesTo` every paper belonging to THIS container is filed under.

importerEntityId.description: The company that owns the goods.

containerNo.description:
The carrier's own container number, as printed on the box — MSCU1234567. Free text: we do not validate
 a format we are not the registrar of.

destPort.description: Where it is cleared — "Djibouti", "Mombasa", or an airport. A label, not a modelled place.

dischargePort.description:
WHERE THE VESSEL PUT IT DOWN, when that is somewhere else — a landlocked import discharged at a
coastal port and cleared inland. Absent means the two are the same place.

mode.description: How the goods arrived. Absent on anything recorded before the field existed — see modeOf().

natureCode.description:
WHAT THE GOODS ARE, in the vocabulary the freight side already uses. The importer's choice.

The distance between a food tank and a fuel tank, and nothing about the container says it. Absent
means nobody has said, which is why the road leg refuses to carry certain combinations blind.

cargoHeightM.description:
How tall the CARGO stands, in metres, where the box has no roof.

Only meaningful for an open top or a flat rack, and it is the difference between the height of the
floor the cargo sits on and the height of the movement. Absent on an open box leaves the road height
unknown rather than guessed at the box's own figure — see standsOn().

tank.description: A tank's last cargoes and its cleaning certificate. The only thing that makes one food-grade.

dangerous.description: The importer's dangerous-goods declaration. Never derived from the goods description.

etaAt.description: Expected arrival, when somebody knows it. NOTHING FILLS THIS AUTOMATICALLY — see the service comment.

etaSource.description: How the arrival information got here. `manual` is the only value anything writes today.

roadFreightId.description:
The road leg, once a person has minted it. Stored as id AND code: the id is what the freight
 machinery answers to, the code is what a human reads on a screen beside this container.

bondedFreightId.description:
BL1 — THE BONDED LEG: the quay to the counter, run before any customs entry is made.

Only a split chain has one. Where a box is discharged and cleared in the same place there is nothing
to move under bond, and the single leg above is the delivery.

releasedAt.description:
BL1 — WHEN CUSTOMS LET IT GO, recorded by the agent who cleared it.

NOT derived from the papers being accepted. An agent accepting a bill of lading is our record of our
own process; a release is a state's decision about the goods, and the two can be days apart. The
delivery leg of a split chain waits on this, because a truck sent to a counter that has not released
the box is a truck sent to wait.

customsHolds.description: CL4 — what the state did to this container. Absent on every consignment recorded before the slice.

key.description: A slug the agent chooses, unique within this consignment — what `supply` and `accept` name.

label.description: The agent's own words: "Investment licence", "Ministry of Agriculture permit".

copies.description: How many physical copies the counter wants. Some of the user's papers were wanted in ten.

documentId.description: What the importer attached. One of THEIR OWN documents, never a file uploaded into this list.

document.description: The attached document, as much of it as this reader may see. Absent until the importer supplies one.

stale.description:
The importer replaced the attached paper with a newer version. We do NOT follow it silently — see the
 service — so the agent is told the version they accepted is no longer the current one.

expired.description: The attached document's expiry has passed. Said before it is relied on, never discovered at the counter.

state.description: `waiting` nobody has supplied it · `supplied` waiting on the agent · `accepted` · `rejected`.

ownerEntityId.description: Whose papers these are — the importer.

readerEntityId.description: Who may read them — the clearing agent. Exactly one company, never a list.

readerName.description:
THE READER'S NAME AND ADDRESS, because an entity id is not an answer to "who can read my papers".

The screen showed `partner-et-djibouti-clearing-lj2ga` — a primary key, wrapped over three lines in a
column too narrow for it. Somebody deciding whether to revoke access to their own commercial papers
was being asked to recognise a slug. The name is what they know the company by; the handle is where
they can go and read who it is before deciding.

Absent where the record has no name for that id, rather than falling back to the id dressed as a
name — an unknown reader is a thing worth seeing plainly.

reaches.description: How many papers this grant actually reaches today. Derived, and it moves as papers are added.

importId.description: Which container, on a `consignment` grant. Absent on a standing one.

code.description: What a person reads it as — IMP-004, FRT-012.

fingerprint.description: sha256 of the bytes. Never called `hash`: the response mask strips that name at every depth.

issuer.description: Who is asking to be paid — the agent, the carrier.

payer.description: Who is asked to pay — the importer, the business.

currency.description: Whatever currency the parties agreed in. Ours to show, never to convert.

reference.description: Their own number for it — the quotation or invoice number on the proforma.

agreedAt.description: The payer agreed to the figure. Not every quotation asks for it; a run's published price was agreed by booking.

paidReference.description: The payment's own reference, as the person confirming it gave it — a bank or mobile-money transaction.

heightM.description:
External height in metres. 2.591 standard, 2.896 high-cube — the 30 cm that decides a bridge.

ABSENT for the four size codes that are OPEN RANGES ("taller than 2896 mm"). The standard declines
to say, so we do too, and the road leg then has no height to give the bridge map.

palletWide.description: The 2.5 m class rather than 8'0" — a box that will not fit some older chassis at all.

group.description: The standard's own grouping — 'tank (dangerous liquids)', 'ventilated', 'flat rack'.

openTop.description: No fixed roof: craned from above, not weatherproof, and the cargo may stand proud of the box.

outOfGauge.description: How tall the movement stands, where the cargo was declared taller than an open box.

heightUnstated.description: True where the CODE does not state a height, so somebody has to measure the box.

by.description: A person's name — or, on the DERIVED account, the leg whose photograph it is.

photoRefs.description: Media ids, readable only through this consignment's own photograph route.

derived.description:
TRUE where this account was read off the leg rather than typed by anybody.

The driver's securement photograph was taken to prove a load was strapped down, and it is being read
as evidence of a container's condition. That is a fair reading, and it is not the same as somebody
standing at the gate and saying so — which is why a reader is told which one they are looking at.

stated.description:
FALSE means nobody has said anything about this gate at all.

Sent as a fact rather than left as an empty list, because a gate with no record is where an argument
gets settled by whoever sounds more certain — and that is the thing this slice exists to prevent.

kind.description: `stopped` has an ending; `unknown` has neither an arrival nor a picked-up road leg.

since.description: What the running clock counts from.

daysElapsed.description: Whole days, floored: a part-day is not a day anybody is charged for, and not one we will invent.

freeDaysBy.description: Whose figure it is. Shown beside the countdown, always.

dueBackAt.description: DERIVED, never stored — a stored due-date goes stale in silence the moment the claim is corrected.

demurrageDays.description: How long it stood inside the terminal before the gate, where both dates are known. Closed, not running.

basis.description: One sentence naming what is being counted and whose numbers these are. Screens show it verbatim.

ownerCode.description: The first three letters are the owner; the fourth says what the equipment is.

cscPlateDate.description:
The date on the CSC safety-approval plate. Carried, with NOTHING stated about it: whether a box is fit
is a surveyor's verdict, and the same line that refused to certify a tank holds here.

timesUsed.description: How many spells out of a terminal this box has had with us — the history a per-consignment record loses.

owedByName.description: WHO OWES THE RETURN: the agent who booked it, derived from the appointment rather than typed.

arrivedAt.description: Recorded by a person — nothing here watches a vessel berth, and we do not guess at an arrival.

outGatedAt.description: DERIVED from the road leg's pickup. The leg we mint is what starts detention, in code and not only in prose.

ending.description:
How the spell ended, and there are two endings rather than one.

`returned` is the one the first draft assumed was the only one. `bought` is the ordinary market case —
containers are traded goods, sold and never returned — and a box that was bought is never overdue.

returnLegCode.description:
Y2 — THE LEG HOME, on the same board as any other load.

Its DELIVERY is what records the return, exactly as the laden leg's pickup is what records the
out-gate: the box is back when the leg that took it back arrived, and nobody has to remember a date.

returnEmpty.description: True where there is nothing in it. Said out loud: an empty run is real work with no cargo to bill.

interchange.description:
Y3 — BOTH GATES, ALWAYS, so the one nobody recorded is visible as the one nobody recorded.

A box handed over with a hole in it and no photograph is a dispute the importer loses by default.

destPort.description: WHERE IT CLEARS. The papers a border asks for are that border's, and this is which border.

dischargePort.description:
WHERE THE VESSEL PUT IT DOWN, when that is somewhere else — a landlocked import discharged at a
coastal port and cleared inland. Absent means the two are the same place.

agentHandle.description: The agent's PUBLIC address — `seebuyget.com/@handle`. An entity id is not somewhere you can go.

youAre.description: Which side of this the reader is on. An operator reading over the network's shoulder is `onlooker`.

accepted.description: Derived every read, never stored: how many of the agent's list are accepted, out of how many.

waitingOnYou.description: Lines waiting on THIS reader to act. What the console counts on the group badge.

feeState.description: CL2b — how far the agent's fee has got. Derived on every read.

roadFreightCode.description: CL2b — the road leg minted from the port, when one has been.

documents.description: The importer's papers this reader may see: their own, or whatever the grants reach.

grants.description: Every grant over these papers, live and revoked, so both sides see what was shared and when.

fee.description: CL2b — the agent's quotation: the figure, the proforma, and open or paid as the parties confirm it.

bondedFreightId.description: BL1 — the bonded run from the quay, where the chain is split.

releasedAt.description: BL1 — when customs released it. Until then a split chain cannot mint its delivery leg.

customsHolds.description: CL4 — what the state did, with both parties' accounts. Shown to both, and to an operator.

cargoGaps.description:
WHAT IS STILL MISSING BEFORE THIS CAN GO ON A TRUCK, in sentences. Derived on every read.

A food tank whose last cargo nobody has stated; hazardous goods with no UN number; an open box with
no cargo height. Each is a fact no code, description or weight can supply, and each makes the road
leg refuse — so it is said on the screen from the moment the container is recorded, rather than
discovered by whoever finally tries to mint one.

containerFacts.description: The container type's own facts, resolved from the catalogue so no screen re-derives them.

box.description:
THE BOX ITSELF, and the clock running on it — Y0 and Y1.

Absent until a container number has been recorded, because the box IS its number: there is nothing to
derive an entity from until somebody names one. Present for both parties, deliberately — the agent
who booked it owes the return and the importer pays for it being late, so hiding the countdown from
either of them would be choosing which one gets surprised.

evidenceMediaId.description: A photograph already uploaded through the media rail. Both gates are checked in the service.

currency.description: Three letters. Absent: the money of the country the goods clear in.

reference.description: The agent's own quotation or proforma number.
The payment's own reference — a bank or mobile-money transaction.

at.description: When it happened, as the party recording it says. Defaults to now.

disputed.description: Of those, how many the other party to that container disputes. Shown with the count, always.

listedLate.description: Containers where the list GREW after the importer had begun supplying — the two-week story, counted.

modes.description:
WHAT THEY HAVE ACTUALLY BEEN SEEN CLEARING, by mode — beside what they SAY they clear.

The two are shown together on purpose and they are allowed to disagree: an agent may advertise air
freight and have no air consignment on our record, which is information rather than a contradiction.
See `recordSays` for the sentence that has to travel with an empty one.

places.description: Ports, airports and border posts they work — labels, exactly as `destPort` is. We run no ports.

words.description: What the vocabulary cannot hold. Their own words, shown as theirs.

measured.description: What was measured and what was not. In the payload so no screen can render the figures without it.

handle.description: Their own public page, so "the same thing a shipper reads" is a claim they can go and check.

offer.description:
THEIR OWN ADVERTISEMENT, returned with their record so the two are one read.

The screen that edits a claim and the screen that shows the record are the same screen, and a form
loaded from a different source than the page a shipper reads is a form that can silently disagree
with it.

certificateDocumentId.description: One of the importer's OWN documents. A file uploaded into here would be a register nobody verifies.

containerNo.description:
The container number, usually typed later than the booking: it arrives with the bill of lading.

CHECKED AND NOT TRUSTED — the service runs the ISO 6346 mod-11 arithmetic and refuses a number that
cannot be right. A field on a service that is not on its DTO is stripped in silence, which is why
this line exists at all.

cscPlateDate.description: The date on the CSC safety-approval plate. Carried, with nothing stated about it.

containerType.description:
ANY ISO 6346 size/type code — not an enum of a shortlist.

Four characters, validated for shape here and RESOLVED by the service against the standard's three
tables. An enum would have frozen the API at whatever subset somebody had seen, which is the mistake
the first version of this made.

cargoHeightM.description: How tall the CARGO stands, for an open box whose own height is only the floor it sits on.

where.description: The depot it went back to, when it was returned. A label a person types, like a port.

fromLabel.description: Taken from the laden leg's destination when we have one; asked for only when we do not.

depotEntityId.description: Y4 — a yard picked from the register, so the box lands on ITS list. Never matched from the label.

weightKg.description:
NO @Min HERE, deliberately — the service owns this rule and answers it in a sentence.

The drive found the reason: a decorator refusing with "weightKg must not be less than 1" shadowed the
only useful thing anybody could say, which is that an empty container is not a light one and its tare
is painted on its door. One rule, in the place that can explain it.

cargo.description: What is in it, if anything. Absent is an EMPTY run, published as one.

visitDays.description: The days visitors are received: `mon` … `sun`. An empty list clears them.

visitFrom.description: From when until when on those days, `HH:MM`. An empty string clears one.

visitHoursByDay.description:
A day of the week with hours of its own: `{ sat: { from: '09:00', to: '12:00' } }`. The object REPLACES the days'
 own hours; an empty one clears them, and a day given null keeps the hours of most days.

closedDates.description:
The dates it is closed: public holidays, one-off closures — or, with `from` and `to`, a shorter day. The list
 REPLACES the list; an empty one clears it.

visitorsPerHour.description: How many visitors it sees in an hour. Zero clears it: then no hour fills.

contactName.description: Who to ask for. A role or a name, whichever the company prefers.

phoneAlt.description: The gate and the office are usually different telephones.

address.description: Where the gate is, in the words a driver needs — not the registered address, which is a legal fact.

hours.description: When somebody is there. The second question a haulier asks, after where.

visitDays.description: The days visitors are received — `mon` … `sun` — and from when until when (`HH:MM`). Theirs to set.

visitHoursByDay.description: A day of the week with hours of its own — `{ sat: { from: '09:00', to: '12:00' } }`. Theirs to set.

closedDates.description:
The dates it is closed — `{ date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', note?, from?, to? }`, shorter rather than closed where it has
 hours — and how many visitors it sees in an hour. Theirs to set.

basis.description: Said out loud on every screen that shows it: this is their claim and nobody checked it.

contact.description: HOW TO REACH THEM — the whole point of a finder, and the thing this one first shipped without.

basis.description: ALPHABETICAL, and said out loud — an ordering is a judgement, and this list makes none.

position.description:
THE YARD'S OWN WORDS for where it is: "C-12, third row". A label so a haulier can be told where to
drive, not a coordinate in a model we pretend to hold.

empty.description: Nothing in it. A yard plans differently for an empty than for a box that has to be stripped.

said.description: What the yard SAYS is standing there.

derived.description: What we DERIVED — legs that ended here. Incomplete by construction: it knows only our own legs.

inbound.description: What is ON ITS WAY here. The one thing a gate man with a notebook cannot know.

inBoth.description: How many appear in both lists. A fact about two sources, never a merge of them.

contact.description: How to reach the yard, written by the yard. Their own entry, on their own screen.

position.description: "C-12, third row" — their handwriting. We record a position; we never assign one.

places.description: Ports, airports and border posts they work — labels. We run no ports and validate none.

handle.description: Their public page. The whole point of a result: somewhere to go and read the rest.

offer.description: What they say they clear, in their own words. Never verified — see ClearanceOffer.

appointed.description: What we have actually seen: appointments and cleared consignments. NEVER a score or a rank.

thin.description: True when the record is too thin to state a usual time. Said, because a newcomer is not a bad agent.

contact.description:
HOW TO REACH THEM — their own entry, published by them and never verified by us.

The finder's whole purpose is that the next step is a telephone call, and it first shipped without a
telephone number. The same card the yard finder and the public page show: one per company.

location.description: A dropped pin. Exactly one of this and `address` is needed; a pin wins where both arrive.

address.description: An address to resolve. Refused where we cannot place it, rather than guessed at.

pickupSiteId.description:
THE PLACES, BY ID. A site carries its own name and point, so the leg stops asking for coordinates.

The raw fields below are still accepted, and only for network staff acting through the API on a
company with no saved places yet. A screen sends ids.

pickupLabel.description: Defaults to the port the container is cleared at.

entityId.description: The sister that owes it. Its books are where the drawdown posts.

payeeDid.description:
WHO IS PAID — the party the network contracts with: a fleet, a courier, a hub. Never a person who
 merely did the work; see DriverService.payeeOf.

day.description:
The settlement day this covers, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

The idempotency key, with the payee: a run that fires twice — a retry, two operators, a cron that
overlaps itself — must not pay the same day's work twice. Same-day settlement is a promise about
WHEN, so the day is the natural unit rather than a batch id nobody can reason about.

providerRef.description: The rail's own reference. The thing you quote when somebody says they were not paid.

entryId.description: The journal entry that moved the money. Present ONLY once settled — before that nothing has moved.

reversalEntryId.description: …and the entry that moved it back, if it bounced.

amount.description: The figure in force, in the company's own currency.

own.description: Whether this company set it. False: it is the figure every company starts from.

totalPct.description: What the customer's price is actually built with — the three, added.

lane.description: The lane this row is about; null is the sister's default for everything it does.
The lane it applies to; absent means the company's default for everything.

by.description: The name the token carried, or the DID when a machine did it. Never a string from a request body.

from.description: The resolved figures before and after, as a short readable line ("2.00% → 3.50%").

maxRatePct.description: The ceiling on ONE layer, and on the three of them added together — they are the same number.

taxRegistration.description: The number this sister collects tax under. Sister-wide: a registration is not a per-lane fact.

topUpFee.description:
What this sister charges a shop or a store to put money in. Sister-wide, like the registration above
and for the same reason: a top-up is not a lane of work, so there is nothing for it to vary by.

ABSENT MEANS NO FEE, and the console has to say so in those words rather than showing zeroes — a
threshold of 0 against a charge of 0 reads like a decision somebody made, and nobody made it.

amounts.description:
What a parcel costs and what each step pays here, every line of it, in this company's currency. Company-wide
like the top-up fee: a wage for shelving a parcel does not vary by lane of work.

lanes.description: The sister's default first, then one row per lane.

recentChanges.description: The most recent changes to this company's terms, newest first. Empty until somebody turns a knob.

transacting.description:
Whether this entity may be a party to a transaction at all. The group may not — it is the merchant of
record nowhere — so its knobs are not editable, and the screen has to say why rather than fail on save.

carrierPapers.description:
Which of a carrier's own papers this sister refuses to trade without. Sister-wide, like the top-up
fee: a transport licence is not a lane of work. Always present, and EMPTY for nearly everybody —
the console says "nothing enforced" in words, because an empty list is a decision that shows.

editable.description: Whether the CALLER may change these, as opposed to only read them — see EntityService.mayAdminister.

name.description: What the audit trail will record against every change this person makes.

twoStepResetAskedBy.description: A reset of their two-step sign-in, asked for by this member of staff and waiting for a second.

passwordLinkUntil.description: They have not chosen a password yet: until when the link emailed to them works (it may be past).

removalFrom.description: The setup key asked to take this sign-in away: from when it can finish, unless a member of staff stops it.

twoStep.description: Whether this account signs in with a code from an authenticator app as well as its password.

until.description: When it stops waiting. Asked for again after that, it waits again.

mine.description: Asked for by whoever is reading this: they can take it back, and cannot approve it.

forSetupKey.description: The one who asked is the only one able to sign in, so there is no second member of staff: the setup key approves.

setupOnly.description:
Said to the SETUP KEY outside a sandbox: this list, and setting staff up from it, is all it reaches. The console
shows that and nothing else, rather than a screen of refusals.

twoStepResetAskedBy.description: A reset of their two-step sign-in, asked for by this member of staff and waiting for a second.

passwordLinkUntil.description: They have not chosen a password yet: until when the link emailed to them works (it may be past).

removalFrom.description: The setup key asked to take this sign-in away: from when it can finish, unless a member of staff stops it.

link.description: IN A SANDBOX ONLY, where no email leaves: the link that was written, so the laptop can be walked through.

sent.description: Whether the email with the link was handed over. When not, it is tried again; a new link can also be sent.

twoStep.description: Whether this account signs in with a code from an authenticator app as well as its password.

lane.description: Which kind of work this applies to. Omitted = the sister's default for everything.

costOfRiskPct.description: What carrying the exposure costs — an insurance premium, or the provision standing in for one.

profitOnRiskPct.description: What the sister earns for choosing to carry it — where a specialised vehicle pays itself back.

marginPct.description: The general company layer, on everything.

freeAbove.description: Top up this much or more and it costs nothing, in the sister's own currency.

amount.description: The flat charge below that threshold. The service refuses one worth a fifth of the threshold or more.

wholesale.description: What a parcel taken in at the counter costs the shop's float. Also the float a shop needs to take one in.

labourFee.description: Paid to a shop for taking in a parcel that was paid for already.

handoverFee.description: Paid to a shop for handing a batch to the driver.

shelvingFee.description: Paid to the receiving shop when the parcel lands on its shelf…

toteLoadFee.description: Paid to a driver for scanning a bag aboard.

mdpSortFee.description: Paid to a hub for each parcel it sorts.

holdingFeePerDay.description: What a day of holding a parcel costs once its free time has ended.

lane.description: Which kind of work this applies to. Omitted = the sister's default for everything.

ratePct.description: As a FRACTION — sixteen percent is 0.16, not 16. Bounds are enforced in the service.

label.description: What the authority calls it: 'VAT', 'GST'. The network has no default worth having.

registration.description: The number this sister collects under. Required before any rate above zero will be accepted.

lane.description: Which kind of work this applies to. Omitted = the sister's default for everything.

premiumPct.description: Charged on the declared value ABOVE the free limit, as a FRACTION — two percent is 0.02.

freeLimit.description: Covered on every shipment without anybody declaring anything, in the sister's own currency.

phone.description:
The number the payment prompt should go to — STK push, the main path the user chose on 2026-09-22.

Optional because the fallback has to keep working: a payer who gives no number is shown a paybill
and a reference, which is how somebody paying from a kiosk or another person's handset pays. Given,
it is the phone that will ring asking for a PIN, so it is TYPED BY THE PAYER rather than read off
their record — the phone that pays is often not the one we have on file.

note.description: Why the fleet wants it. Read by the operator deciding whether to publish.
Why this line — read by the operator deciding whether to publish it.

natureCode.description: S30 — the commodity's primary cargo nature (default GEN). Drives the compatibility matrix.

state.description: Open until an operator decides. This is the field that makes `Disputed` a queue rather than a grave.

fromStatus.description:
The status the parcel held when the dispute was raised, restored when the case closes. Stored
 rather than inferred: a rejected counter dispute must leave the parcel collectable again, and
 guessing that from the origin would be one assumption away from stranding somebody's goods.

raisedBy.description: Who reported it — an agent DID at a counter, a person DID from the app.

award.description:
What was awarded, in the parcel's own currency. Zero on a rejection, and zero is a real answer
 that still gets recorded — a refusal a claimant can be shown beats a case that went quiet.

note.description:
The operator's reasoning. REQUIRED on every decision including a rejection: a person whose goods
 arrived broken is owed an explanation even when they are not owed money.

currency.description:
The money the award is in: the parcel's own where it names one, otherwise that of the company whose books
 carry the award. Stamped at the decision — a parcel taken in at a counter names no currency of its own, and
 the sender was once told "40.00  is owed to you". Absent on a rejection.

atId.description: Whose place it was: an agent DID, a vendorId, or the sender's own DID.

originAgentDid.description:
The first PUDO to take custody — absent when there is none, which is a real case rather than missing
data: a store collected from its own dock hands the parcel straight to a driver. This is NOT where the
parcel came from; that is `birthplace`, which every parcel has. The two were one field until they had
to be told apart.

collectingEntityId.description:
R1 — the sister company that collects for this shipment: the one in the PAYER's jurisdiction. A
vendor order is paid by the store, so it is the store's sister; a walk-up is paid at the counter,
so it is the origin shop's. Never the group, which is not a party to customer transactions.
Internal: it is an accounting fact, and appears on no consumer or public surface.

takeInPromise.description:
WHO ANSWERS FOR THESE GOODS — decided when they were taken in, and kept.

  ours    a sister carries it: our cover, our claim, our money. The shop is OUR agent.
  theirs  no sister can, so a carrier prices it, is paid for it and answers for it, while we
          record custody and prove it. There is no collecting entity and no posting of ours.

Stamped on the parcel rather than derived later, because a country’s standing can change while
goods are on a shelf, and the promise made at the counter is the promise that was made.

otp.description:
Release secret. The destination agent reads it aloud from their screen and the customer repeats
it back — it is never SMS'd, so it costs nothing and works with no signal. Because it is the
sole custody check, wrong attempts are counted and the code is burned at OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS.

otpAttempts.description:
Wrong-attempt counter for whichever release secret this parcel uses — the OTP above on a peer-send,
the collectionCode below on an inbound order. A parcel has exactly one live secret, so one budget
guards both paths; it is reset when the secret becomes live (arrive() / shelve()) and by a reissue.
