otpLockedAt.description: Set when the release secret was burned by repeated wrong attempts; release needs an operator reissue.

transportFactor.description:
The SIZE FACTOR its transport was quoted at, stamped at mint for the same reason. A network constant
 today, but one that will be retuned — and the flexible rebate recomputes the real cost at delivery,
 so an unstamped factor would re-price parcels already sold. Absent on records written before this
 field existed; read it through ParcelService.transportFactorOf, which falls back to the constant.

intakeCharge.description:
What the shop was CHARGED for this parcel at its counter (before tax), and what it was PAID for taking it in — by
its own company's list on that day. Kept because both are taken back if the parcel is cancelled, and a list that
changed in between must not make what comes back differ from what went.

shipmentProvision.description:
The COST-OF-RISK slice of the platform fee on this shipment — money set aside against claims rather
than earned, stamped at mint like everything else about the price.

Inside `platformFee`, never on top of it: the customer paid this the day the rate stack shipped, and
moving it from revenue to a provision changes no price. Stamped because a sister that turns its
cost-of-risk knob tomorrow must not change what was set aside for a shipment sold today — and
because a refund has to release exactly what a billing set aside.

Absent means ZERO, the same reading as tax: a shipment sold before any of this carried no cover.

declaredValue.description:
THE COVER on this shipment, stamped at mint.

`coverLimit` is the ceiling an upheld damage award is checked against — the free limit the selling
sister carries, or the value the shipper declared, whichever is higher. Declaring less than the free
limit does not reduce cover: the floor is a floor, not a swap.

`shipmentPremium` is what was charged for the part above the free limit, and like the cost-of-risk
slice it accrues to the claims provision rather than to revenue — money collected against a promise,
not earned for a service performed.

Stamped, so a sister that changes its policy tomorrow cannot change what it promised on a shipment
sold today. Absent on every parcel from before this existed, which reads as NO cover — the honest
answer, because none was priced, promised or paid for.

currency.description:
The money every figure above is in — the SELLING sister's, stamped at mint. Absent on records
 written before prices named their unit; read it through `parcelCurrency` (parcel.service.ts).

customs.description:
The paperwork this parcel crosses a border with. Absent on a domestic shipment, which needs none —
 and never absent on one that crosses, because the mint refuses to sell that shipment without it.

sellerEntityId.description:
The sister that SOLD this shipment: it collected the price and carries the cost of every leg, so a
 shop in another country that handles this parcel recharges its own sister's outlay to this one, at
 cost. Absent on records written before a parcel named its seller — then nobody recharges anybody,
 which is exactly right for a single-sister world.

fx.description:
The exchange rates this parcel's price was struck at, when it needed any.

 Kept for the same reason `platformFeePct` is: a price is a promise made at a moment, and the rate
 behind it moves. Without this, a cross-border parcel's cost is a number nobody can reconstruct or
 argue about, and the sister that collected it could not later prove what it owed the sister that
 performed the leg. Absent on every domestic parcel, because nothing was converted.

ceilingProvision.description:
…and the cover inside that ceiling, for the same reason: the rebate has to release exactly the
 provision the ceiling set aside, and re-deriving it from a rate would land a cent away.

readyAt.description:
When it became collectable — the moment it hit the destination shelf.

Stamped rather than derived from the last scan, and the difference is not cosmetic: a wrong
collection code writes a `Ready_For_Pickup` scan of its own, so ageing off the scan list would reset
the uncollected clock every time somebody fumbled their code. The one event that matters here happens
once, so it is recorded once.

Absent on records written before this existed; readers fall back to the scan list.

uncollectedRemindedAt.description:
When the receiver was reminded it was still waiting. Set once — see the dispatcher for why one
 reminder and not a series — and set even when there was nobody to tell, so somebody who signs up
 later is not greeted by a nudge about a parcel that has been sitting a fortnight.

lateToldAt.description:
When the people on it were told it is running late (see runningLate). Once, and set even when there was nobody
 to tell, for the same reason as the reminder above.

returnParcelId.description:
The journey home, for a parcel nobody came for. Present only on a 'Returned' one — the two read as
 one story rather than as an abandonment and an unexplained new shipment.

unclaimedAt.description:
When the free collection window ran out — the start of the holding-fee clock.

Distinct from readyAt, and the distinction is the whole feature: readyAt is when the wait began,
this is when the wait stopped being free. An extension resets readyAt and CLEARS this, because a
receiver who bought more time is inside a free window again by definition.

holdingSettled.description: Holding already settled, so a part-paid parcel is not billed twice at the counter.

holdingFeePerDay.description:
What a day of holding costs, fixed when the free time ended (the list of the company whose shop holds it, that
day). The days already owed are not re-priced by a later change to that list. Cleared with `unclaimedAt`.

extensionsUsed.description: Extensions taken. The first is free (FREE_EXTENSIONS); counted so the second can be priced.

receiverResponse.description:
What the receiver said when told the window had closed. Absent means silence — which is the
 common case and an outcome the whole flow has to reach correctly without.

collectProxy.description:
Somebody named to collect instead of the receiver. Their code releases the parcel; so does the
 receiver's own, because nominating a neighbour does not stop you collecting it yourself.

relinquishedAt.description:
When the RECEIVER gave up their claim to the goods.

Only the receiver can set this: sender owns the shipment, receiver owns the goods, so the receiver
is the only party with anything to relinquish. It does not make the box disappear — there is a real
parcel in a real shop — and it is not 'Voided', which would say the shipment never happened when it
happened all the way. It moves the parcel into the disposal queue, and only once no store still has
a funded claim to bring it home.

birthplace.description: Where it came into being. Absent on pre-slice records — read it through `birthplaceOf`.

custody.description: Who has physically held it, in order. Absent on pre-slice records — read through `custodianOf`.

plan.description:
THE PROMISE, KEPT — the route it should take and when it should be ready to collect, as planned the moment it
entered custody at its first shop (JourneyPlanService). Frozen then and never rewritten, so it can be held
against what happened (`planVsActual`). The tracking page used to work its plan out again at every read, and a
promise worked out afresh every time is always on time. Absent where no route could be planned.

packaging.description:
FB5 — how the goods are PACKED, which decides the body and what has to lift it. Omitted falls back to
 the DEPLOYMENT's default (sacks here, loose in a European deployment), never to a network-wide guess.

excludedBodies.description:
FB2d — bodies the SHIPPER rules out. At a counter the walk-in customer IS the shipper, so this is their
 call to make and the clerk's job only to record it. A PREFERENCE, not a limit of any vehicle: the board
 shows it as the shipper's choice, and it binds a claim only because the driver was told first.

instructions.description: FP7 — CMR box 13 at the counter: instructions for the door, a contact to dial, a delivery window.

bodyHint.description:
FB2c — what the shop THINKS the load needs. ADVISORY by decision: recorded, shown and counted, never
 matched on, because a clerk cannot reliably tell a skeletal from a flatbed and a binding wrong pick
 would exclude the one operator who could have carried it.

insurer.description: Null takes the insurer off the policy.

recoverAboveValue.description:
The goods value above which this store wants an uncollected parcel shipped back to it. Omitted =
 never offer; 0 = always ask. Two different statements, and both are real.

ownerPhone.description:
The store operator's phone (S20). When present, this vendor is linked to the operator's person
 identity so the same human can also send, receive or drive under one account — never a duplicate.

email.description:
THE STORE'S OWN ACCOUNT: the email and the password its people sign in to the Store app with. Given together.
A store registered without them (by a script, by an integration) sets them up the first time somebody signs in.

callbackCarriesCode.description: Include the collection code in the ready_for_pickup callback (default true — see Vendor).

country.description: The country the dock stands in. Omitted = the store's own — a warehouse abroad says so.

sealRequired.description:
A SHOP bag, published by the shopkeeper's SEAL and by nothing else. A hub bag has no seal step, so the
dispatch sweep publishes it the moment it is full or aged; a shop bag that the sweep published behind
the counter would advertise a bag still open on the floor — and lock the shop out of the completeness
gate, which only accepts a filling bag. The sweep asks the shop to close it instead (see publishReady).
Undefined on a hub bag and on every pre-slice record, which is the correct default for both.

sealPromptedFor.description: Which nudge this shop has already had for this bag, so the sweep asks once per reason (full → aged).

sealedAt.description: When the shop closed it. The record that the completeness gate ran, distinct from being published.

haul.description:
What carrying this bag is worth, LOCKED AT CLAIM — the tote analogue of a freight's `lockedPrice`.

Locked rather than computed at delivery for the same reason freight locks: the driver agreed to a job
whose distance and contents were what they were at that moment. A parcel added after they claimed, or a
destination re-pointed by a re-sort, must not silently rewrite what they are owed either way.

Absent on a bag nobody claimed through the marketplace (it can still be loaded), and on every record
written before this existed — both settle on the handling fee alone, and `basis` says which.

fromAgentDid.description: Where it is now — the shop holding it — and where it would go back to.

declaredValue.description: What the goods are worth, and what the journey home costs. The store's arithmetic, shown not implied.

holdingCost.description:
What the shop is owed for having held the slot since the window closed — recomputed on every read,
never stamped.

The transport half is a held price a store is billed exactly what it was shown. This half is a
METER, and showing it as though it were fixed would be the one dishonest number on the screen. It
grows while they think about it, which is also the truest pressure this feature has: a store
watching the cost of deciding nothing go up is being told something real.

quoteId.description: The held price this will be billed at. A store is billed the figure it was shown.

returnParcelId.description: The return shipment, once it exists.

did.description: Real GLOS DID (S2). The mdpId stays the domain key; the DID is what an actor token binds to.

country.description:
The country this hub stands in — same fact as a shop's, and it matters more here: a hub is where a
 cross-border journey changes hands, so the leg into it is the one that clears customs. Absent on
 pre-slice records; read it through MdpService.countryOf.

entityId.description:
The sister company this hub is contracted to — same reasoning as a shop's: a fixed site sits in
 one country. Absent on pre-entity records; read it through MdpService.entityIdOf().

insuranceExpiresAt.description: FP4 — a passed insurance expiry takes the vehicle OFF THE ROAD (see papers.ts); no date recorded switches nothing off.

inspectionRef.description: FP4 — the roadworthiness / inspection certificate, enforced the same way.

kind.description: READ from papers.ts rather than restated here — a second copy of an enum is a second thing to forget.

daysLeft.description: Whole days until it lapses — negative once it has. Absent without a date.

toteCapacity.description:
How many BAGS the hold takes — the constraint kilos cannot express (a tote of letters weighs nothing, so
by weight a bus fits a hundred while its boot holds a dozen). Absent on vehicles registered before this
existed: read it through DispatchService.toteCapacityOf, never off the field.

ownerDriverDid.description:
WHOSE OWN VEHICLE THIS IS when no fleet owns it — the courier who registered it at signup, and the only
driver who may start a shift on it. Absent on a fleet's vehicle (`managerDid` says whose) and on vehicles
registered before this existed.

papers.description: FP4 — DERIVED on the owner's read, never stored: each paper's state today.

offRoad.description: DERIVED: every reason it cannot start a shift, in words — its papers, then its upkeep. Empty: it can.

upkeep.description: DERIVED on the owner's read, never stored: the reasons besides its papers — in the workshop, a defect, a service overdue.

notes.description: DERIVED on the owner's read: what to know that does not keep it off the road — a service due soon.

incoterm.description: CL1 — the trade term the parties agreed, and the place it names. Selected from the eleven, never invented.

instructions.description:
FP8 — box 13 for an order that ships as freight: what the driver needs at the door, and when. No contact —
 the goods go to a shop, whose counter is the contact. Ignored for a parcel-sized order, which has no box 13.

natureCode.description: S30 — the commodity's primary cargo nature (default GEN). Drives the compatibility matrix.

says.description: The promise spelled out, because a public reader has no other way to know what the word means.

what.description: What was checked, in words — 'trading licence', not 'kyc_licence'.

keptRate.description: Null while the record is thin — three loads shows three loads and no average.

inFlight.description: Neither delivered nor handed back — running. Not a success and not a failure.

tightKept.description: Loads they kept that nobody else would take for two days: scarcity work.

ratesNeed.description: How many loads a rate needs, so a screen can say so without knowing the server's config.

formerly.description:
The name the handle was derived from, present ONLY when it no longer matches `name`.

A handle does not follow a rename (that would be a rotted link and a way to inherit somebody else's
page), so when the two diverge a reader is entitled to see both rather than wonder why the address
says one thing and the heading another.

country.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 where they stand. Absent for the group company, which stands nowhere in particular.

at.description: A coarse pin, for the kinds that have a place a customer walks to. Never a street address.

area.description: The zone or town, in the words the record uses.

presence.description:
HOW ESTABLISHED THE NETWORK IS WHERE THEY STAND, and what that does and does not promise.

Carried because the page is public and a reader has no other way to know it: `matched` means we hold
no money there, and cover is zero by construction where nothing can pay a claim.

ABSENT WHEN WE DO NOT KNOW WHICH COUNTRY THEY ARE IN, and that is the whole reason this is optional.
The presence service answers `observed` for an unknown jurisdiction, which is correct for the ladder
and a lie on a page: it renders as "we only observe this country" about a country nobody named. A
fleet with no jurisdiction on its record, and the group company that stands nowhere in particular,
both hit that. Found by reading the page rather than the code — the sentence was plausible and wrong.

verified.description:
What the network has VERIFIED about them, and when. Empty is a real answer and shows as one.

Never a badge and never a score: the list is what staff checked, so a reader can weigh it themselves
rather than trusting a tick.

onRecord.description:
What the company has put on record ITSELF, with the paper, since it was switched on — and which NOBODY HERE HAS
CHECKED. Kept apart from `verified` on purpose: listed together, the page would be vouching for a paper no member
of staff has looked at. It counts, and anybody connected to the company who can see the paper may report it.

moves.description:
CL4 — THE MOBILISATION RECORD: whether they find and move trucks.

On the PUBLIC page on purpose. An operator-only signal does not remove our influence over who gets
appointed, it conceals it: work still gets steered by suggestion, and nobody outside can audit a
nudge. The shipper sees it because the shipper is the one choosing, and the party sees exactly the
same fields at the same moment — a record handed down is a verdict, one both parties hold is an
account.

Absent for a kind that does not mobilise anything (a shop, a hub) rather than present and zero. The
counts are always real; the RATES are null while the record is thin, because five stars from three
loads is the same untruth as hiding them.

movesMeasured.description:
What we measured, and what we did NOT — carried in the payload so no screen can render the figures
without the sentence. This measure's failure mode is being read as a general endorsement.

clears.description:
CL4 item 1 — THE CLEARANCE RECORD, for a company that has been appointed to clear a container.

The same class the agent's own route returns, so their copy and a shipper's view cannot differ: a
record handed down is a verdict, one both parties hold is an account.

What is NOT in it is the point. There is no border-time figure anywhere, because scoring an agent on
elapsed time at a counter systematically advertises whoever pays bribes, and absence of a seizure is
not evidence of compliance. `holds` carries what the STATE did, counted apart, labelled, disputable
by the other party to that container, and never netted off the agent's own figures.

Absent for a company that has never been appointed, rather than present and zero.

offer.description:
WHAT THEY SAY THEY CLEAR — their own advertisement, and the only asserted thing on this page.

Everything else here is derived from the record, which is what makes the page trustworthy. This is
not, and it must be shown as what it is: a dated claim by the company itself, unchecked. It exists
because nobody else could know it — an agent who specialises in air freight or vehicles cannot be
discovered by observation until somebody has already hired them for it.

recordSays.description:
WHY AN EMPTY RECORD IS NOT A BAD RECORD.

We count only the consignments that came through this network, and most of an agent's business never
will. Carried in the payload beside the counts, because a reader who takes silence for incompetence
has been misled by us about our own coverage.

contact.description:
HOW TO REACH THEM — the company's own entry, written and published by them.

Only for a COMPANY, and deliberately not for a shop or a hub: those pages carry a coarse pin and
never a street address, which is a consumer-safety choice this must not undo from the side. A yard or
a clearing agent publishing its own gate number and opening hours is a different act — it is a
business asking to be telephoned, and the directory's whole point is that somebody can.

Never verified. The `basis` sentence says so on the page.

handle.description: The handle, without the '@'. Immutable once issued, and derived from the verified name.

name.description: The trading name as the record holds it now — which may differ from what the handle came from.

since.description: On the network since. The one number that is honest from day one.

does.description: What this participant does here, in plain words — never a capability list a reader must decode.

code.description: The load, by its code — an operator can look it up.

driver.description: The driver's shop-floor label, never their legal name. Operators are trusted, not omniscient.

handle.description: Their public page, so an operator can read exactly what a shipper reads.

drivers.description: How many drivers they field — the denominator behind everything below.

measured.description: What the figures do and do not cover — the same sentence the public page carries, verbatim.

country.description: The country the hub stands in. A hub may serve zones across a border; it stands in one country.

driverBadgeId.description: What the shop or hub scanned on the driver's phone. A driver loading a bag themselves sends none: it goes onto their own badge.

jurisdiction.description: Country of incorporation (ISO-3166-alpha-2) — the sister that contracts and pays this fleet.

enteredBy.description: The member of staff who put them on record, by name. Somebody ELSE approves them.

licenceExpiresAt.description: When the transport-operator licence runs out. Its NUMBER stays on `requirements`, where it always was.

licenceCopyRef.description:
WHAT EACH DATE WAS READ FROM: the document the fleet sent, once staff recorded a date off it. Absent
means the date was typed on somebody's word — and never the OLD document left beside a NEW date.

insurancePolicy.description: Goods-in-transit / carrier liability cover: the policy and its expiry.

recordedBy.description:
Who typed these dates and when — the same provenance a driver's licence carries, and for the same
reason: a screen must be able to say whether a date was read off a document or taken on somebody's word.

sent.description:
A RENEWED DOCUMENT THE FLEET SENT, waiting for somebody here to read it — one per paper.

The date on it is the FLEET'S reading and switches nothing on: the paper on record changes only when a
member of staff types the date they read off the same image. Same rule as a courier's renewed licence.

refused.description: Why the last document sent for a paper was not accepted — shown to the fleet so it knows what to send.

jurisdiction.description:
Country of incorporation — which sister company contracts and pays this fleet, and in what
currency. A fleet is paid as a SUPPLIER, one invoice in one currency; how it then pays its own
drivers, in which countries, under whose employment law, is entirely the fleet's business.

entityId.description:
That sister, by id. Absent on records written before entities existed — read it through
 FleetManagerService.entityIdOf(), which resolves from the jurisdiction.

papers.description: The operator's own papers and their expiry dates — recorded always, enforced only where a sister says so.

timeZone.description:
The time zone the office keeps, where it has said so. Most fleets never do: a fleet in a country with one time
zone is on that zone's clock without anybody typing it. Read it through FleetManagerService.clockOf().

code.description: The fleet code — or `did`, the fleet chosen after phone + PIN (fleet/managers/mine). Either only names the fleet.

device.description: The key this device was handed when a code to the phone was typed on it. Without it the PIN is not looked at.
The key this device was handed when a code to the phone was typed on it. Without it the PIN is not looked at.

proof.description: The two drivers at the vehicle together, proven by the code of the one handing over — or the carrier's office's word.

aboard.description: The goods were aboard (taken over) when they moved; otherwise the truck coming to collect them changed.

by.description: Who recorded it: the driver who took the goods over, or the office.

window.description: The window the plan was made to, as it was read then — kept, because the shipper may reword what it asked for.

lateMin.description: Planned to arrive this many minutes after the window its shipper asked for.

earlyMin.description: Planned to be handed over this many minutes before its window opens.

held.description: Set when its trip came up and it could not be put on the truck. Cleared when it is, or when the day is planned again.

seq.description: Its place in the trip's round, from 1.

arrive.description: When the truck is expected at the door, on the clock.

offeredTo.description: The partners still deciding. A partner that declines is taken off; nobody left means the offer has run out.

via.description:
PASSED ON. The partner that took it from the fleet it was ordered from, and passed it on to the one carrying it
now (`partner`). One step and no further: a fleet that an order was passed on to carries it or gives it back.

onward.description: While the partner that took it is offering it on, and nobody has taken it yet. It is in nobody's plan meanwhile.

rootId.description: The order as it was placed: the id and code of its first load.

no.description: This load, and how many there are.

at.description: When it was split, and by whom in the carrier's office.

otherDay.description: Handed over on another day than it was ordered for: before it, or after it.

window.description: The window asked for, as it read at the handover. Absent: none was asked for, or it was not written as hours.

lateMin.description: Minutes after the window closed, or before it opened. Neither, with a window and on its day: inside it.

timeZone.description: The carrier's time zone it was read on.

day.description: The day and the time of the handover, on that clock.

truckSubtype.description: The truck body. Absent for a vehicle class that has no subtype — a van is a van.

heightM.description:
HOW TALL THE LOAD STANDS ON A DECK, in metres — the half the bridge map never had.

`dimensionsCm` cannot answer this: it is orientation-free by design, so nothing can tell which of the
three numbers is the height. Dispatch has carried a comment since the hazard map shipped explaining
why it passed NO height at all — "a 4.0 m load is 5.2 m on a flatbed and 4.4 m on a lowboy" — and
this is one of the two numbers that comment was waiting for. The other is the vehicle's deck.

Absent means unknown, and unknown stays HEIGHT_UNKNOWN against a low bridge rather than becoming a
pass. A 40ft high-cube sets it from the container catalogue; an open top sets it from the declared
cargo height, because the box's own figure is the floor the cargo sits on.

bodyHint.description:
The minter's own body pick. ADVISORY — shown, compared and counted, NEVER used to filter (user, 2026-08-30).
 A shop clerk booking a walk-up cannot reliably tell a skeletal from a flatbed, and a binding wrong pick
 would invisibly exclude the one operator who could have taken the load. Where it disagrees with the
 derived body, that disagreement is itself a market signal worth reporting.

excludedBodies.description:
Bodies the SHIPPER rules out — theft risk, an insurer's wording, a customer's requirement. A PREFERENCE,
 and typed as one: the board says "the shipper ruled out open bodies", never dressing it up as physics.

packaging.description:
FB5 — how the goods are PRESENTED for handling, which is what decides the body and the kit.

Recorded per consignment rather than inferred from the commodity, because the same commodity is handled
completely differently from place to place (user, 2026-08-30): sugar is poured into a food-grade bulk
trailer in Holland and stacked in sacks on a flatbed in Kenya. A rule keyed on "is it sugar" gets one of
those two wrong wherever it is deployed.

pickupCountry.description: CA6 — the country at each end, where it is known (a shop's), so the rules of crossing can be asked.

reloads.description:
Moved to other vehicles of the carrier after a breakdown, oldest first: what the consignment note writes in box 18.
The vehicle the goods are in now is the last one moved to while aboard; the one they were taken over in stays on
`carriage`, as the note's carrier box says.

cancelledAt.description: FP3 — withdrawn by the sender (or the network) before the goods were taken over. Terminal; the record stays.

deliveryAttempts.description: FP3b — every time the driver stood at the door and could not hand over. The load stays in transit.

claim.description: FP3b — the sender's claim against the delivered goods, and how it ended. One per load.

priceOrigin.description:
FB0c — where lockedPrice came from. 'computed' (or absent, for anything locked before FB0c) means it IS
 priceBreakdown.total. 'negotiated' means two parties agreed a number, so lockedPrice is authoritative and
 may differ from the breakdown — which is kept anyway, because its distances are real and are what the
 market series reads. Every money path already reads lockedPrice; nothing bills off the breakdown.

settlement.description:
B2 — WHO SETTLES THIS HAUL, stamped when it is posted and never re-derived.

`between_parties`: the shipper pays the carrier directly, or through its own payment network, and nothing is
accrued for the carrier on any of our books at delivery. Every load a customer's business posts is this (the
user, 2026-10-04: "we don't handle their payments at all"). Absent: the network's older rule — a carrier we
contract with is owed their earning on delivery whoever the shipper was.

postedByName.description: Which person in a business posted it — the business's DID is shared by everybody in it.

onBehalfOf.description: B4 — the client an expeditor sent this for, as their agent. The client is the SENDER on the note. A copy, not a link.

contract.description:
P1 — the standing contract this order was placed under: which fleet must carry it, for whom. A copy, stamped when
it was ordered, so the papers never change if either side renames itself or the contract later ends.

deliverOn.description: P1 — the calendar day a contract order must ARRIVE. What the fleet plans against, and what makes it late.

orderRef.description:
P1b — the SHIPPER's own number for this order (a webshop's order number). Kept apart from `externalOrderId`, which
names a shop order or a consignment and makes the consignee "the buyer of order …, collecting at a shop". Under one
contract a number is used once: it is what makes uploading the same sheet twice harmless.

planned.description:
P3 — the truck and trip this order is on in the plan its fleet accepted for its day. A plan, not a fact about the
goods: it goes on a driver only when the office sends that trip out. Rewritten when the day is planned again.

handOn.description:
P4 — what became of an order its fleet could not carry itself: offered to its partners, taken by one, or released
to the open board. Absent: the fleet it was ordered from carries it.

handedBack.description: P4 — each time a partner that had taken it gave it back before collecting: who, why, when.

partOf.description: One load of an order that comes in several. Absent: the order is in one load.

rejoinedInto.description: A load that was put back together with the rest of its order: the id of the order. It is in no list from then on.

deliveryTiming.description: Read at the handover and kept: when it was delivered on its carrier's clock, against the day and window asked for.

commitMode.description:
FB0c — how this load may be taken. 'instant' (the default, and what every pre-FB0c load is read as) means
 a fit driver claims it at the computed price. 'negotiate' means the minter wants to agree a price first:
 drivers PROPOSE, the poster accepts one, and only that acceptance claims the load.

postedCurrency.description:
THE MONEY ITS POSTER SET THE BUDGET IN — its poster’s company’s (a shop’s, a store’s, a business’s, a fleet’s), stamped
when it is posted and never re-derived. The budget, the prices offered on it, the one agreed and any refund or award
its poster is told of are in it. The carrier’s side has its own (`lockedCurrency`, frozen at the claim). Absent where
no company of ours settles its poster, or nobody posted it: then its figures are the bare ones that were typed.

carrierDid.description:
THE CARRIER OF RECORD — the party the network contracted with when the job was taken: the driver's fleet,
or the driver themselves when they drive for nobody. Fixed at the claim, like the price and the body.

Only the driver used to be recorded, so "whose job was this" was answered from the driver's fleet TODAY.
The day a driver can move to another fleet that answer changes under every haul they ever did: the old
fleet's earnings statement — the list its payday is reconciled against — loses them, and the new fleet
reads a competitor's customers and prices. A history keyed to the present is not a history.
Absent on a load claimed before it was recorded, which is read from the driver as it always was.

incoterm.description: FP8 — every time a driver gave this load back before pickup: who, why, when. The load went back on the market.

handBacks.description: Each hand-back names the driver and the carrier they gave it back for (absent on one recorded before that was kept).

instructions.description: FP7 — CMR box 13, as given at posting (or edited before the goods were taken over).

instructionAmendments.description: FP7 — subsequent instructions, given while the goods are on the road. Appended, never overwritten.

indivisible.description:
Can the load be split into two smaller ones? The single most decision-changing fact about anything
 oversize: a divisible 30 t is two ordinary trips, an indivisible 30 t is a low-loader and a permit.

bodyDerived.description:
FB0b — the body this load canonically needs, STAMPED at registration (and the basis it was derived on).
 Frozen rather than computed on read for the same reason a price is frozen at claim: "kilometres of
 flatbed offered in 2026" must not change when someone tunes a threshold in 2027. Absent on a pre-FB0b
 freight, which is derived live and reports itself as weight-only.

bulk.description:
DERIVED from packaging (`loose`), and kept because vehicle matching is written against it.

It used to be the stored truth and it meant two opposite things — "loose, it tips or augers" in the body
derivation, "sugar/cement bags" in the vehicle spec. It now has exactly one meaning, the loose one, which
is what `Vehicle.carriesBulk` and the board's NO_BULK_BODY blocker already assumed.

equipmentGaps.description:
S32c — the ends whose SITE cannot handle this cargo (no qualifying load/unload equipment on hand). An
 ADVISORY flag ("arrange a forklift at the destination"), not a block — a Local Admin resolves it. Empty
 when both ends are equipped (or their equipment is unknown, e.g. a bulletin freight with only geo labels).

containerNo.description:
Y2 — THE BOX THIS LEG IS CARRYING, where the load is a container rather than goods in one.

Kept on the leg as well as on the box because the board reads it: a haulier deciding whether to take
a run wants to know it is a box going home, and a driver wants to know before they arrive.

emptyRun.description:
TRUE WHERE THERE IS NOTHING IN IT — an empty container being repositioned.

Said out loud rather than inferred from a small weight, and never dressed up as freight: an empty run
is real work with no cargo to bill, and a board that quietly published it as a load would be lying to
the driver who takes it. The weight is the box's own tare, which is painted on its door.

bonded.description:
UNDER BOND — the goods are in the country and have not entered it.

A container discharged at a coastal port and cleared inland travels the first leg before any customs
entry is made: no duty has been paid, and the movement runs under a transporter's transit licence
with a bond standing behind what would be owed if the box never arrived. It is a different job from
the delivery that follows release, and only a carrier licensed for it may take it.

`bondCountry` is where that licence has to be held, which is the country the leg runs inside.

lockedCurrency.description:
The money `lockedPrice` is in, frozen with it at the claim: that of the company paying the carrier then. A
 carrier can move to a fleet in another country, and a price read in today's money would change its meaning
 after the fact. Absent where no company of ours pays the carrier, and on a haul locked before this existed —
 read then, as it always was, in the network's money.

postedByDid.description:
FB0c — who posted the load, and therefore who negotiates for it. Distinct from shipperDid, which is who
 PAYS: a counter booking deliberately has no shipperDid (the customer's cash settles off-platform) yet
 still has a shop that must be able to answer a proposal. Absent for a bulletin freight → operators only.

carriedBy.description:
FB4a — what actually CARRIED it, stamped at claim. The mirror of `bodyDerived`: that one records the body
the load needed, this one the body that turned up.

Frozen for exactly the reason the derived body and the price are frozen. Only `claimedBy` was ever
recorded, so "kilometres moved by container chassis in 2026" could only be answered by looking up what
that driver is coupled to TODAY — and a driver who sells a flatbed and buys a box van would silently
rewrite every haul they have ever done. A market series that changes retroactively is not a series.

Absent on a load claimed before FB4a, and on one whose claimer had no truck subtype (a van or a bus).
Such a haul is counted as UNKNOWN in the analytics, never attributed to a body by inference.

reason.description: Why not — required when refusing: whoever puts the papers on record again reads it.

insuranceExpiresAt.description: FP4 — YYYY-MM-DD; the day after it, the vehicle is off the road until renewed.

deckM.description:
How high the loading deck stands, in metres — the other half of a bridge check.

Declared, because only the fleet can measure it and a class average would clear a load under a bridge
on arithmetic about somebody else's truck. Absent leaves the hazard map answering HEIGHT_UNKNOWN,
which is the truth.

insuranceExpiresAt.description: FP4 — YYYY-MM-DD; the day after it, the vehicle is off the road until renewed.

jurisdiction.description:
Legal residence (ISO-3166-alpha-2) — for an INDEPENDENT courier, who the network pays directly.
 Ignored when managerDid is set: the fleet is paid, and its drivers are the fleet's business.

truckSubtype.description: A truck's body, which a truck is registered with.

country.description: Where they legally reside: it decides the company of ours that would contract them.

idCopyRef.description: Their own photographs, sent with the ask: the ID card and the driving licence staff read.

note.description: The fleet's own words — required when the reason is `other`, shown to the driver.

by.description: The manager who did it, for the fleet's own record.

recordedBy.description: Who recorded the current date, and when. Absent on dates recorded before this was kept.

courierAsk.description:
IN NO FLEET, AND ASKING TO RIDE FOR THEMSELVES on a van, a truck or anything heavier than a motorcycle — which a
courier does only once network staff have read their ID and licence and checked their record. Waits in the queue
staff already have (Joining the network) until decided; cleared then, or the moment they take a fleet’s place.

portrait.description: Their face, for the badge — see DriverPortrait. Absent is ordinary, never a blocker.

jurisdiction.description:
Legal residence — and ONLY for an independent courier, who the network contracts with directly.
A fleet-attached driver has none, deliberately: the network pays their fleet, not them, so asking
where they live would be collecting data for a payment we never make. We move parcels; we do not
do payroll or employment. Read through DriverService.settlingEntityIdOf(), which sends a fleet
driver's answer to their fleet.

entityId.description: The sister that contracts this courier directly. Absent for a fleet-attached driver.

licenceRenewal.description: A renewed licence sent for checking — see LicenceRenewal. Cleared when it is recorded or refused.

nudgeMinEarn.description:
Do not interrupt this driver for work paying less than this, all in.

It lives on the DRIVER, not on the coupling, unlike the snooze and the derived-leg switch beside it.
Those two are moods held for a shift — a puncture, a favour taken this morning — and it is right that
ending the shift ends them. A fee floor is not a mood: it is the driver's cost base, and fuel does not
get cheaper because yesterday finished. Asking for it again every morning would make it the thing it
replaced — a number typed into a search box that dies on the next reload.

The price of standing is that it can starve somebody silently, which is exactly what the snooze warns
about. That is paid for by COUNTING what it suppresses and showing them (see DispatchService's floor
report): a setting you can watch working is a setting you can undo.

Absent, or zero, means no floor. Bounded by MAX_NUDGE_MIN_EARN.

papers.description: FP4 — DERIVED on read: the licence's state today; non-empty offRoad means no shift can start.

device.description: The key this device was handed when a code to the phone was typed on it. Without it the PIN is not looked at.

fromCompany.description: The fleet they drive for now — absent for a courier on their own, or a driver between fleets.

blockers.description: Each thing to finish first, as a sentence the driver can act on. Empty means they can say yes now.

runs.description: The runs of that fleet they were on and are now off.

country.description: ISO country code of where they legally reside: it decides the company of ours that contracts them.

truckSubtype.description: A truck's body — a truck is registered with one.

idCopyRef.description: Anything heavier than a motorcycle: their own photographs of their ID card and their driving licence, for staff to read.

driverName.description: Only once they said yes — until then a phone number names nobody to the office.

note.description: The fleet's own words — required for `other`.

licenceNumber.description: A renewed licence can carry a new number. Omitted leaves the number on record alone.

by.description: Who is recording it, for a console on the shared key; a named sign-in's own name wins.

settleMethod.description:
How the shipper pays the fleet — a RECORD, never a posting. Required of a new run: a price with no
way to pay it is the hole this closes. Optional here only because the same shape reads back records
declared before it existed.

vehicleId.description: Which truck. Required: a run that names no vehicle is selling a number somebody typed.

capacityKg.description: How much of the vehicle is for sale. Absent means all of it — the registry already knows.

capacityM3.description: Cubic metres of hold. Absent where the fleet has not measured it — then only weight can bind.

coverLimit.description:
WHAT THE CARRIER’S OWN POLICY COVERS, per load. Zero is a real answer — "I carry none" is exactly
what a forwarder needs to hear, and a different fact from a carrier who has not said.

coverPolicy.description: The insurer and policy, as the carrier writes it. What a forwarder rings to verify.

minCharge.description: The least the run will take. What stopping and strapping down already cost.

freeMin.description:
Waiting time, and it is both or neither. `waitingPerHour` without `freeMin` is refused by the service:
billing from the moment the truck arrives is a surcharge on loading, not a charge for a delay.

km.description: Required when charging by the kilometre — otherwise every booking prices at nothing.

amount.description: In the currency of the country the fleet stands in.

minCharge.description:
The least this departure will take, whatever the arithmetic says.

Not a detail: on every basis except `per_trip` a small booking can price at almost nothing, and a
carrier who has stopped, opened the back and strapped something down has already spent the expensive
part of the job. Optional, because a flat trip price needs no floor.

freeMin.description: Minutes at each stop that are simply part of the job.

perHour.description: Per hour beyond the free window, pro rata, in the departure's currency.

limit.description: What their goods-in-transit policy pays up to, per load, in the run's currency. Zero means none.

policy.description: The insurer and policy, as the carrier writes it. What a forwarder rings to verify.

note.description: The carrier's own words: required for `other`, optional beside any coded reason.

constraintId.description: The hazard report filed with it, when the carrier put a closure on the map.

note.description: The carrier's own words: required for `other`, optional beside any coded reason.

receiverName.description: Who took the goods, in their own name. Two characters minimum — "x" is not a receiver.

photoRef.description: A photograph of the goods as put down. A mediaId, adopted from the driver’s own upload.

remarks.description: Anything the driver wants on the record — a reservation, a remark, a note about the state.

confirmed.description: The unload checklist keys they confirmed.

by.description: Who tapped it — the driver at the door, or the office closing a run off a bad signal.

photoRef.description: The shipper’s own photograph of what arrived. Beside the carrier’s two, not instead of them.

amount.description: What they say it cost them, in the run’s currency. Their figure, like the declared value.

answer.description:
WHAT THE CARRIER SAID BACK, which is the half that makes this a record rather than an accusation.

`accepted` and `refused` are the carrier’s own words about their own liability — never ours, and
never binding through us. Absent means they have not answered yet, which is itself a fact worth
being able to point at.

freeAt.description: When it was free to go. Absent while the driver is still standing there.

waitedMin.description: Total minutes on site, free window included. Kept so the charge can be re-read rather than trusted.

billableMin.description: Minutes beyond the free window — the only ones that cost anything.

amount.description: What those minutes came to. Zero while the wait is still ordinary, and zero when waived.

bearer.description:
WHO IT LANDS ON, spelled out rather than inferred at reading time: `shipper` for a delay at loading,
`consignee` for one at delivery. Stored because the attribution is the feature.

waivedReason.description: Set when the fleet let it go, with their reason. A waived charge stays visible: it happened.

arrivedAt.description: When the vehicle presented itself. Until this exists there is no clock and nothing is owed.

kind.description:
WHOSE LOAD THIS IS — and it is the difference between a marketplace and a run sheet.

 `sold`  a shipper found this departure in the offer list and took the space. We quoted it, they
         agreed to it, and both sides can read the same price for the same reason.
 `own`   the fleet already had this customer long before it came anywhere near us. Nothing here was
         sold, priced or promised by this network; the fleet is telling us the load exists so that
         the space it fills stops being advertised to somebody else.

F4, and the reason F3 is usable at all. A fleet with a book of business had two options and both were
bad: stay off the offer list, or publish capacity it has not got. The second ends with a shipper
standing at a gate beside a truck that was full before they booked it.

bookedByName.description: B2 — which person in a business booked it: the business's DID is shared by everybody in it.

trackingKey.description:
The key behind this booking's public tracking link — the same link format and page as a load's. Only on space
somebody bought (`sold`): a fleet's own customer is not ours to hand a link to. Absent on bookings made before.

onBehalfOf.description: B4 — the client an expeditor sent this for, as their agent. The client is the SENDER on the note. A copy, not a link.

customer.description:
THE FLEET'S OWN CUSTOMER, in whatever name the fleet files them under. Only on `own`, and required
there: a load with no customer against it is not a booking, it is a hole in the capacity that nobody
can account for a week later.

A name and not an account, because the whole point is that these people are not here. In a country
where we only match, the fleet IS the local operator and arrives carrying its customers with it.

It never leaves the fleet's own screens. A shipper reading the offer list learns how full the truck
is and not one thing about who else is on it.

freightId.description: The load itself, where one exists on the board. Absent for space bought ahead of the goods.

volumeM3.description: Cubic metres, where the shipper measured. See `binds` for why both axes are kept.

nature.description:
WHAT THE GOODS ARE, in the vocabulary the board already uses.

A booking used to be a free-text description, a weight and a volume — which meant hazmat could be put
on a food-grade tanker and nothing anywhere would notice. The board has known better since S30: a
nature maps to a vehicle capability, and a load is never offered to a vehicle that lacks it.

The same rule, on the same enum, because a shipper who has learned what FOP means on one screen has
learned it on all of them — and because a second vocabulary for the same fact is how two halves of a
product drift into disagreeing about whether a load may travel.

declaredValue.description:
WHAT IT IS WORTH, as the shipper declares it. Optional and never verified.

Not a valuation and not a promise: it is the number a forwarder needs to arrange cover, the number a
claim is argued against, and the number that makes "the carrier's policy stops at 200,000" mean
something rather than nothing. Absent is a real answer — plenty of loads are not worth insuring.

binds.description:
WHICH AXIS ACTUALLY FILLED THE TRUCK for this booking — 'weight' or 'space'.

Recorded rather than derived later, because it is the whole argument for why the price was what it
was, and a fleet reading a past run deserves to see that the load which cost them the trip was the
light one. It is also the honest answer to "why did my pallet of foam cost that".

price.description:
What it was quoted at, on the departure's basis, in the departure's currency.

On an `own` load this is whatever the fleet said they charge, and zero where they did not say. It is
their figure for their own run sheet: we did not quote it, we do not hold anybody to it, and no ledger
moves because of it. Which is why every screen keeps it apart from what was sold here.

units.description: What the basis was applied to — kilometres, kilograms, or 1 for a trip. Kept so the price can be re-read.

status.description:
WHERE THIS LOAD GOT TO, and the third state is the one the model was missing.

A run used to go open → departed and then stop. The goods reached a door, somebody took them, and no
record of that existed anywhere — while the rest of this product is meticulous about custody. The
waiting clock even had the driver standing at the DELIVERY gate tapping, which proved the truck got
there and never that the load came off it.

 `booked`     aboard, or going to be
 `delivered`  handed over, by the driver who was standing there
 `cancelled`  given back before it travelled, by the shipper or the fleet

cancellation.description: Set when `cancelled`: which side gave it back, and the carrier's reason. Absent on bookings given back before it was kept.

deliveredAt.description: When it was handed over. The server's clock, like the gate taps, and for the same reason.

pod.description:
PROOF, at the standard the board already holds a delivery to.

This used to be an optional name and nothing else, which made the same act — a driver handing goods
to somebody at a door — provable on a board haul and unprovable on a run. A shipper discovering that
asymmetry after a load went missing would be right to feel misled, and the fix is not to soften the
board: it is to hold this to the same line. A name AND a photograph, because "delivered" without
either is the driver’s word against the sender’s, and with them it is box 24 of a consignment note.

It is the DRIVER this protects first, which is the part worth remembering when it feels like a
burden at a gate in the rain.

receivedBy.description: Who took it. Kept flat as well as on the proof, because every screen reads this one line.

loadSafety.description:
WHAT THE DRIVER CONFIRMED AT LOADING — the securement half, which the board also has.

A load that arrives broken is argued about at the OTHER end of the journey, and the photograph that
settles it was taken hours earlier. Recorded at the loading gate, where the driver is already
standing and already tapping.

claim.description: What the shipper says went wrong, and what the carrier said back. Never decided by us.

waiting.description:
THE CLOCKS, one per stop, and empty on a run where nothing went wrong.

Kept on the BOOKING rather than the departure because a shared truck waits for one shipper at a time:
three loads on the same run, and the two-hour stand at the second collection belongs to the second
shipper alone. A departure-level total would be exactly the unattributable number this exists to avoid.

shipperDid.description:
Who bought the space — a store, a shop, a person. Whoever the freight belongs to.

On an `own` load this is the FLEET's own DID, because the fleet is the party answerable to us for what
is on their truck and their customer has no account here to name. Who it is actually for is `customer`.

reloads.description: Went on in other trucks after breakdowns, oldest first: what its bookings' consignment notes write in box 18.

capacityM3.description:
Cubic metres, still DECLARED rather than derived: the vehicle registry holds a weight and no volume,
so there is nothing to read it from. Left that way rather than guessed from the class, because a
box body and a flatbed of the same tonnage are not the same offer.

waiting.description:
What happens when the truck is kept standing. Absent means the fleet does not charge for waiting —
see `WaitingTerms`, and note that absent is FREE rather than unlimited-and-unspoken.

settle.description:
How the shipper pays the fleet. Required of every new run; absent on records declared before this
existed, and a screen reading absence says the fleet has not said rather than inventing an answer.

cover.description:
What the CARRIER's own insurance covers, where they have said. Absent means they have not said, which
a screen reports as exactly that — never as "covered" and never as "not covered".

km.description: The distance the line runs, where it is known — what `per_km` is multiplied by.

driverDid.description:
WHO IS DRIVING IT, once the fleet has said.

Not decoration: the waiting clock is recorded by the person standing at the gate, so without this there
is no one holding a phone who is allowed to start it. A departure with no driver yet is ordinary — the
fleet sells the space first and rosters later — and nothing about it can be clocked until there is one.

note.description: What the fleet wants a shipper to know: a tail-lift, a reefer, "no hazmat".

status.description:
open       taking bookings
closed     the fleet stopped selling, and what is booked still travels
departed   it has gone
cancelled  the run is not happening, and everybody booked on it has to be told

departedAt.description: When the fleet said it had left. Stamped once, at that moment — what a tracking page counts "under way" from.

cancelledReason.description:
Why it was called off, kept rather than only announced.

The notice goes out once, the day it happens; the shipper looking at the wreckage of their week a
fortnight later is reading this screen, not their notifications. Required when anybody was aboard.

cancellation.description:
The same, structured: the coded reason the apps translate, the carrier's words, and the hazard report
filed with it. `cancelledReason` stays as the sentence, because the consignment note prints English.

corridorId.description: The fleet's own published line. Only its owner may put a departure on it.

leavesAt.description: When the vehicle actually goes. The one fact a shipper plans around.

vehicleId.description:
WHAT IS FOR SALE, ON BOTH AXES, because whichever runs out first is what "full" means.

A truck is not a number of kilograms. The parcel side of this product worked that out already and
prices a parcel on `max(kg, volume / divisor)`; this is the same fact at truck scale. A fleet that
declared only kilograms would sell four tonnes of tempex it cannot physically fit, and one that
declared only cubic metres would sell a load of steel that breaks its axle.

Space is optional: a fleet that has not measured its hold says nothing rather than guessing, and then
only weight binds — which is stated on the booking rather than assumed.

plate.description: What a shipper and a gate actually recognise. Copied at declaration, like the line name.

capacityKg.description:
What is for sale, which is at most what the vehicle holds.

DERIVED BY DEFAULT and capped always: a fleet may sell less than the whole truck — a genuine choice,
and since F4 usually expressed by recording their own load instead — but never more than it has.

nature.description: What the goods are. The fleet’s own customer’s load can clash with what is already aboard too.

customer.description: Whose it is, in the fleet's own words.

charge.description: What the fleet charges them, for the fleet's own run sheet. We quote nothing and post nothing.

reason.description:
Why, and required by the SERVICE when anybody is aboard rather than by this class.

Optional here because the same route closes a run and marks it gone, and neither of those owes
anybody an explanation. Calling off a loaded run does, and that is a rule about the run's state —
which a DTO cannot see.

note.description: The carrier's own words: required for `other`, optional beside any coded reason.

closureAt.description:
WHERE the road or border is closed, when the carrier puts it on the hazard map. Optional — a carrier who
knows the road is shut but not where exactly still calls the run off honestly — and accepted only with
`road_closed` or `border_closed`. It files an ordinary hazard report, under the ordinary rules.

nature.description:
WHAT THE GOODS ARE, in the board’s own vocabulary — the thing a free-text description could never
say. Absent means general dry, which is most freight; what is refused is a value nobody agreed on.

declaredValue.description: What it is worth, as the shipper declares it. Never verified, and never a promise of ours.

freightId.description: A load already on the board, where this is space for one.

forClientId.description: B4 — an expeditor booking it for one of its clients, as their agent. A business sign-in only.

receiverName.description: Who took the goods, in their own name. Two characters minimum — "x" is not a receiver.

photoRef.description: A mediaId for the photograph of the goods as put down. The driver’s own, unattached upload.

remarks.description: Anything worth putting on the record — a reservation, a remark about the state of the goods.

photoRef.description: Their own photograph of what arrived — beside the carrier’s two, not instead of them.

amount.description: What they say it cost them. Their figure, like the declared value: never verified by us.

note.description: Required on a refusal: a refusal with no reason is not an answer the other side can act on.

photoRef.description: The driver's face for their badge — optional by design; see DriverPortrait.

criminalRecordClear.description:
The record check, recorded BY THE PERSON WHO DID IT, at the moment they approve.

A fleet asserts this when it registers its own driver. Nobody asserted it for a courier who
registered themselves, so `criminalRecordClear` stayed false and approval was blocked for ever with
no way to unblock it — the last locked door on the independent path. It is deliberately not something
the applicant can tick: a self-declared clear record is not a check, and the whole point of this gate
is that somebody looked.

reason.description: Required when refusing: the driver is shown it, and is the only person who can put it right.

snoozedUntil.description:
New offers are SNOOZED until this instant (absent = taking work).

A rider needs this far more than a line-haul driver does: lunch, a fare of their own, a puncture, the
last hour of a long day. It stops NEW work only — everything already claimed is still theirs to carry,
hand over and deliver, because snoozing offers is not going off shift. It lives on the coupling, so
ending the shift ends it: nobody discovers tomorrow morning that they are still snoozed.

derivedLegOff.description:
The driver has switched OFF the road we worked out from the load they took.

One decision, honoured for the rest of the shift. Without it, turning it off would clear a road that
the very next claim puts straight back — which is not a switch, it is an argument. Like the snooze
beside it, it lives on the coupling, so ending the shift ends it.

pin.description:
The driver's PIN — required when they start their OWN shift. A phone left signed in is not proof of who is
holding it, and the start of a shift is where the network records who is driving which vehicle.

leg.description: The leg for this shift, declared in the same breath as picking the vehicle.

odometerKm.description: What the odometer says as the shift starts, in whole km. Checked before the shift starts: lower than the last is refused.

incoterm.description: CL1 — the trade term the parties agreed, and the place it names. Selected from the eleven, never invented.

packaging.description:
FB5 — how the goods are PACKED, which decides the body and what has to lift it. Omitted falls back to
 the DEPLOYMENT's default (sacks here, loose in a European deployment), never to a network-wide guess.

excludedBodies.description:
Bodies the SHIPPER rules out (theft risk, an insurer's wording, a customer's requirement). A stated
 preference, not a physical constraint, and the board presents it as one.

commitMode.description:
FB0c — 'negotiate' posts the load for a price to be agreed BEFORE anyone commits: drivers send their
 number, the poster accepts one, and only that acceptance claims it. Absent = 'instant', the behaviour
 every load has had until now. A negotiate load is deliberately kept out of the push offers and nudges,
 which exist to be answered with a single Claim tap.

buyerMobile.description:
CL1 — who the goods are FOR. The service has always accepted it and this DTO never offered it, so a
 load posted through this route recorded no receiver at all. That was harmless while only the sender
 could claim; it stops being harmless the moment a term can put the loss on the receiver, because the
 party with standing then has no way to be recognised.

instructions.description: FP7 — CMR box 13 at posting: instructions for the door, a contact to dial, a delivery window.

pickupCountry.description: CA6 — the country at each end, where the poster knows it; the rules of crossing are only asked of a known country.

dimensionsCm.description:
FB0b — the load's measurements. Optional: loose bulk genuinely has none (a tipper-load of sand has a
 weight and no shape), and a bulletin freight may be posted before anyone has measured it. Supplied, they
 are STORED — until FB0b they were read to classify the cargo and then discarded, which is why nothing
 downstream could answer "does this fit a flatbed rather than a box body".

indivisible.description:
Can it be split into two smaller loads? A divisible 30 t is two ordinary trips; an indivisible 30 t is a
 low-loader and a permit.

bodyHint.description:
The minter's own body pick — ADVISORY. Recorded and shown, never used to match: a wrong pick would
 silently exclude the operator who could have taken the load.

natureCode.description: S32 — the freight's primary cargo nature (default GEN); drives the required vehicle capability.

scheduledPickupAt.description:
F1 — a FUTURE pickup date: the load is booked for later. Must be a full datetime WITH an offset (Z or
 ±HH:MM) so the instant is unambiguous — a date-only or offset-less string would resolve to a server-
 timezone-dependent moment. Absent = ship now.

allowEarlyClaim.description:
F1 — the shipper's early-claim choice for a scheduled load: true (default) → a driver may RESERVE it
 ahead of its pickup date; false → it stays out of the marketplace until due.

forClientId.description: B4 — an expeditor posting it for one of its clients, as their agent. A business sign-in only.

contractId.description:
P1 — order it under a standing contract: it goes to that fleet's queue and onto no market. A business sign-in, on a
contract it has linked. `deliverOn` is then required — the day it must arrive, today or later.

orderRef.description: P1b — the shipper's own number for an order under a contract. Used once per contract.

code.description: Stable machine code — a screen switches on this, never on the message.

message.description: The English sentence. Not yet translated; the codes exist so it can be, without moving the logic.

bodyDerived.description: What body the load needs, and how strong that claim is (measured, or guessed from weight alone).

deadheadKm.description: The empty run to reach it, the paid run, and their sum — the numbers the whole decision turns on.

price.description: Indicative, priced against THIS driver's vehicle. Absent when they are not coupled to one.

earningsPerKm.description:
Earnings per TOTAL kilometre, empty run included — the board's sort key. Null when it cannot be computed
 (no vehicle, or a zero-distance job): an unsortable row is shown as unsortable, never floated to the top.

canTake.description: True when nothing but an 'unknown' stands in the way.

deliveryWindow.description: FP7 — the sender's delivery window, the one instruction a dispatcher decides against. Never the contact.

containerNo.description: Y2 — the container this leg carries, where the load IS a box.

emptyRun.description:
Y2 — an empty box going home. Real work, no cargo, and it says so on the board rather than reading
 like freight with a suspiciously small weight.

bonded.description:
BL1 — uncleared goods, carried under a transit licence. Said on the board, because a driver who
 cannot take it is entitled to know that before tapping it, and one who can should see the job.

value.description:
Metres for a height, kilograms for a limit. Required for the kinds that have something to measure —
 the service refuses those without it, because an unmeasured limit cannot be checked against a load.

photoRef.description:
A media id of the thing itself — the bridge, the washout, the sign.

OPTIONAL, and that is the design rather than laziness: a driver at a washout at night who cannot
safely stop must still be able to warn everybody, and a photograph as a gate would suppress reports
exactly where they matter most. A report with no photo warns identically; the picture is what an
OPERATOR later clears or keeps the hazard on.
The media id of what they photographed, when they did. Fetchable by an operator.

disputedAt.description:
When somebody first said it was gone. Absent unless the status is 'disputed'.

The operator's queue is sorted on this and not on the report date: a bridge reported two years ago and
disputed this morning has been waiting for an operator since this morning. Sorting the queue by the
report date would bury today's dispute under every old hazard on the map.

accounts.description:
WHAT EACH SIDE ACTUALLY SAID, in order, with no identities.

The counts above say how many; this says what. An operator deciding whether a bridge is still
standing is doing exactly one thing — weighing one account against another — and until now the
screen handed them two numbers and a merged sentence. `photoRef` is a media id the operator can
fetch; every other reader gets the field and a refusal, which is the media route's rule and not
this module's to bend.

confirmations.description: How many OTHER drivers have since agreed it is there. Never who they are.

refutations.description: How many say it is gone. Recorded and shown, and deliberately not enough to clear it.

photoRef.description: A photo of the road now clear — the strongest thing anybody can offer for the dangerous direction.

by.description: An operator may name the human who made the call; otherwise the token speaks for itself.

requiredEquipment.description: Kit a vehicle must have to load and unload it — the other half of the investment question.

area.description:
Coarse: the nearest town we know, not the pickup's own label. Absent where nothing is near enough
 to name honestly — a distance with no name beats a name that implies precision we do not have.

destArea.description: Likewise for the far end: what corridor this load runs, in towns.

pickupAbout.description: Rounded to ~0.05° (≈5 km) so the market can be mapped without a load being met at its gate.

bodyDerived.description:
The body this load needs and how strong that claim is. THE field the whole page exists for: it is what
 turns "there is work here" into "there is work here for a flatbed".

deadheadKm.description: From the point the caller asked about — their question, not ours.

indicativeTotal.description:
INDICATIVE ONLY, and named so. Computed at the network's default rate for a typical vehicle, because
 an anonymous caller has no vehicle whose rate card we could price against. What an actual operator
 earns is their own rate on their own corridor — this is the market's shape, not an offer.

indicativePerKm.description: Indicative earnings per TOTAL kilometre, empty run included. Null when it cannot be computed.

basis.description:
Said in the payload, not just in the docs: every price here is the network default applied to this
 load, so a client cannot render these numbers as an offer without stepping over the word.

offeredLoads.description: Loads POSTED in the window whose derived body is this one.

offeredKm.description: Their LOADED kilometres — pickup → dropoff. Work asked for; empty running is never in here.

offeredMeasured.description:
How many of those had a MEASURED body rather than one guessed from weight. The rest still count; they
 are a softer claim, and a reader investing against this is entitled to know the difference.

movedLoads.description: Loads CLAIMED in the window and carried by a vehicle of this body.

movedKm.description: Their loaded kilometres. THE number — "km of containers moved".

deadheadKm.description:
The empty run to reach that work. Beside movedKm, never inside it: a market whose fleet turns 40% of its
 wheels empty is a different investment from one that does not, and only a separate figure says so.

day.description: The day these counts fell in, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.

claimedLoads.description: Loads CLAIMED on this day — not necessarily the same loads.

fromPoint.description:
Where the two ends are, so a lane can be drawn and a radius can be measured.

ABSENT WHERE THE END IS 'unknown' — a load more than 60 km from anywhere the gazetteer knows has no
honest place name and therefore no honest dot, and a lane with one is still a real lane. The reader
must keep it in the list and say it cannot be placed, never drop it for being unplottable.

These are the gazetteer's CENTROIDS, not the loads' own coordinates. Two different lanes inside one
neighbourhood share a dot, which is the coarsening working rather than the map failing.

quiet.description: Posting fell materially against the window before, and both windows are above the thin threshold.

unmetLoads.description:
Loads posted in the window that NOTHING ever claimed — demand the fleet did not meet. The gap between
 this and the moved figures is the sentence somebody deciding what to buy is actually paying for.

cancelledLoads.description:
CL3 — posted in the window and then WITHDRAWN by the shipper. Counted here and excluded from unmet,
 because a load nobody was asked to carry is not demand the fleet failed to meet.

metLoads.description:
CL3 — posted in the window, still standing, and claimed by somebody at some point.

The ONLY figure that completes the posted population: `offeredLoads` = metLoads + unmetLoads +
cancelledLoads, exactly, always. `movedLoads` cannot do that job and must not be read as if it could —
it counts loads CLAIMED in the window whenever they were posted, so it answers a different question over
a different population. Both are real (see `buildSeries`), but only this one partitions what was asked
for, and a screen that shows moved beside unmet and withdrawn invites a reader to add three numbers that
come to more than the total above them.

medianHours.description: Median hours from posting to claim. Null when nothing was claimed in the window.

priorMedianHours.description: The same figure for the window of equal length immediately before this one.

stretching.description:
True only when BOTH windows have a median, BOTH are above the thin threshold, and it has lengthened
 materially. A claim this strong is never made on a guess.

thin.description:
Either window is too small to carry the claim. The figures are still shown; the flag says how far to
 trust them.

loads.description: Loads with a negotiated price AND a computed one to compare it against.

medianRatio.description: Median agreed ÷ computed. Above 1 means shippers paid over the stack to get a truck.

from.description:
The window these figures cover, echoed as ISO instants. A kilometre count means nothing without the
 period it accrued over, and "yearly km" is a rate a reader has to be able to check for themselves.

handle.description: Their page at /@handle. Absent only where the directory has not issued one yet.

loads.description: Loads on this lane claimed by them inside the window.

claimedLoads.description: Every load on this lane that was CLAIMED in the window — the sum the rows below are drawn from.

unattributedLoads.description:
Loads whose claim stamped no carriage at all — no fleet and no driver.

It should be zero. It is carried anyway so the rows above always add up to `claimedLoads`, which is
how anybody would notice if it stopped being zero.

basis.description: One sentence naming what was counted, shown verbatim. A list with no basis reads as a ranking.

window.description: The window the plan was made to, as it read it.

partOf.description: One load of an order its carrier split into several.

outsideWindow.description: The carrier's accepted plan has it outside the window asked for. Absent when it is inside it, or not planned.

plannedAbout.description: About when the carrier's accepted plan has it at the door, while it is still on its way. Absent: not planned.

leftOut.description: The carrier's accepted plan for its day leaves it on no vehicle. Gone once a plan has it on one.

runningLate.description: Not delivered, and wrong on its carrier's own clock: on no vehicle on its day, its planned hour passed, or its whole day.

deliveryTiming.description: Delivered: when, on the carrier's clock, and where that fell against the day and the window asked for.

currency.description: The money the budget, the prices offered and the one agreed are in: the poster’s company’s (Freight.postedCurrency).

onBehalfOf.description: B4 — the client an expeditor sent this for, as their agent. The client is the SENDER on the note. A copy, not a link.

contract.description: P1 — ordered under a standing contract: with which fleet, and the day it must arrive.

noteId.description: Its consignment note's id in the archive, once a copy is kept there (from taking over on): what its links hang on.

attempts.description: FP3b — the door the driver stood at and could not hand over at, most recent last.

claim.description: FP3b — the sender's claim, as far as it has got.

incoterm.description: FP8 — the times a driver handed this load back before pickup, most recent last. Reason and time only.

instructions.description: FP7 — the sender's own instructions, and whether they can still be rewritten (before pickup) or only added to.

maxSpend.description: The cash cap the customer agreed — what a price is judged against.

openProposals.description: How many prices are waiting for an answer. The whole reason this row is on a screen.

agreedPrice.description: Set once the load is taken, so the poster sees the outcome without a second call.

pickedUpAt.description: FP3 — the journey's stamps, so the list can say "on the road since", "delivered to", "cancelled".

receiverName.description: FP3 — who signed for the goods (box 24), once delivered.

canCancel.description: FP3 — true while the sender may still withdraw the load: before the goods are taken over.

trackingKey.description: FP6 — the shareable key behind the tracking link, and the link itself, so the shipper can hand it on.

canRate.description: FP6 — true while the shipper may rate: delivered, within the rating window. Re-rating is allowed (last wins).

canClaim.description: FP3b — true while the sender may still claim: delivered, no claim yet, within the claim window.

price.description: The DRIVER's earning being asked for (not the shipper's all-in charge).

note.description: The case for the number, in the driver's own words.

price.description: The DRIVER's earning they are asking for — the same quantity as lockedPrice, not the shipper's charge.

note.description: The driver's case for the number, in their own words ("I'm empty-running past your gate on Thursday").

deadheadKm.description:
The two legs AS AT the proposal, from the position the driver proposed from. Carried so the accepted
 haul records a real deadhead/loaded split rather than one invented at acceptance time.

reservations.description: FP3 — at pickup: the carrier's reservations about the goods as handed over (box 18).

receiverName.description: FP3 — at delivery: who received the goods, the photo of them as put down, and what the receiver said (box 24).

refunded.description: The charge handed back to a billed sender, when there was one.

pathStyle.description: Path style is the default; virtual-host style is the exception AWS allows.

note.description: The note as it was exported (copies/NN-stage.json). Canonicalised and hashed here.

recorded.description: False where nobody has recorded the crossing: the driver is told that, rather than told nothing.

border.description: CA6 — for a load that crosses a border: where it may cross, when, what to carry, and the limits.

destLocation.description:
Where the load is going, as a place — so a driver can see and navigate the whole leg rather than only
 the trip to the pickup. Absent when the destination cannot be resolved to a coordinate.

collectMin.description:
WHAT THIS JOB COSTS THE DRIVER, IN MINUTES — the two figures a decision at the wheel is actually made
on, and the pair `detourKm` could never give.

`collectMin` is the extra time to go and get it. `deliverMin` is the extra time that CARRYING it then
costs, on top of that — because a pickup next door whose destination is an hour the wrong way is not a
small job, and a kilometre figure computed over the pickup alone said it was.

Time rather than distance because that is the unit a driver spends and the only one they can explain
