to anybody else: a bus driver cannot justify eight kilometres to a bus full of passengers, but "this
costs you six minutes" is a sentence everybody in the vehicle understands.

Both are measured against the road the driver DECLARED, so they are genuinely extra. With no declared
road there is nothing to be extra to, and they report the plain travel time instead — which is the
honest reading: when you have no plan, all of it is extra.

`deliverMin` is absent when the destination cannot be placed. Never guessed: a made-up minute is worse
than a missing one, because this is the number somebody agrees to.

price.description:
S34 — the priced offer: the driver's earning + the transparent B + D·R·M breakdown. FREIGHT ONLY —
 a bag has no B + D·R·M, so read `earn` for the figure that covers both kinds.

earn.description:
WHAT THIS JOB PAYS, all in — the one number the driver is agreeing to, for either kind of load.

Freight: the same figure as `price.total`. A bag: the handling fee plus the road it will travel.

It exists because a bag's pay stopped being a constant. Every surface used to hard-code the flat
loading fee, which was true then and became a LIE the moment distance and contents entered the
arithmetic — understating a real job on the very screen where somebody says yes to it. Indicative
here, against this driver's current vehicle; locked at claim, exactly as a freight's price is.

parcels.description:
BAGS ONLY — what the earning is made of: how many parcels are inside, and how full the bag is. See
 Claimable.parcels for why a figure without them is a figure taken on trust.

device.description:
The key this device already holds for this number, if it has one. A PIN replaced on a device the PIN already
worked on needs the code to the phone; on any other it needs the code to the recovery email as well.

email.description:
The recovery email — needed the first time a PIN is chosen, with the code sent to it. It is how somebody gets
back in when their number is gone, and where we warn them. Not asked again once one is confirmed.

inviteToken.description: S24: if the person arrived via an invite link, credit the inviter on first join.

device.description: The key this device was handed when a code to the phone was typed on it. Without it the PIN is not looked at.
The key this device was handed when a code to the phone was typed on it. Without it the PIN is not looked at.

expectedTotal.description:
The locked total the sender consented to at the quote step. If the market moved before mint, the
 server rejects with PRICE_CHANGED (carrying the fresh total) so the app can re-confirm — never
 silently bill a different amount than the one shown.

oldPhone.description: The number the account is on — the one they can no longer use.

newPhone.description: The number it should move to. Already confirmed by a code (auth/phone/request + verify).

nationalId.description: The national ID number they registered with, where they did: a driver's, a shopkeeper's.

note.description: What happened, in their own words. For the member of staff who reads it.

lapsesAt.description: While it waits: when it lapses if nobody decides it.

reason.description: Refused: why, in staff's words for the person.

with.description: A driver's fleet, where they drive for one.

email.description: The recovery email, masked. The asker says they cannot read it.

pinUsedSince.description: The PIN was used — or chosen again by a code to the number — AFTER this was asked. The asker said they could do neither.

numberChangedAt.description: The number was changed less than a day ago, and that can still be undone.

nationalIdOnRecord.description: A driver or shop record on it was registered with a national ID.

stoppedBy.description: Stopped from the account itself: its `holder` said no, signed in — or its `pin` was used after this was asked.

checkedByYou.description: The member of staff reading this is the one who checked it, so cannot be the one to approve it.

namesAccount.description: The old number names an account. False: there is nothing to move, and the request can only be refused.

waiting.description: How many wait on a member of staff.

what.description: What was checked, and how: the ID seen, the questions answered. Kept on the request.

by.description: Sandbox only: the name of the member of staff, where the shared key is in use.

reason.description: Written for the person who asked: they read it with their reference.

nationalId.description: The number on their own ID card — the one registration refused.

phone.description: Their phone number, already confirmed by a code (auth/phone/request + verify).

from.description: With both, the date is not closed but SHORTER: visitors from `from` until `to` that day only.

visitDays.description: The days it receives visitors (`mon` … `sun`), set by the company itself. Absent: it has set none.

visitFrom.description: From when until when on those days, `HH:MM`.

visitHoursByDay.description: A day of the week with hours of its own (`{ sat: { from, to } }`), where the company gave one.

visitorsPerHour.description: How many visitors it sees in an hour, where it has said. With it, an appointment is for an hour.

closedDates.description: The dates it is closed: public holidays, one-off closures.

photosBy.description: Their photographs are due by then.

at.description: The hour — from `at` until `until`, `HH:MM` — where the company counts its visitors by the hour.

offDay.description: The company has since changed its days, hours or closures, and this day or hour no longer fits them.

reference.description: Their own reference: what they say at the desk.

yours.description: This person made the appointment. False: the other did, and this one may come too.

changesLeft.description: How many more times the day can be changed, by whoever made it.

willRemind.description: They will be reminded the day before, in the app and by email — or cannot be: they have no account to reach.

until.description: When it ends: an hour later, or at closing time for the last part of an hour.

photos.description: Which of their three photographs are in.

photosDueBy.description: They may send, or send again, now — and until when.

retakeWhy.description: Staff asked for the photographs again, and why.

yours.description: Decided: the ID is theirs. Absent until there is a decision.

reason.description: Why, in staff's words — written for the one who did not get it.

held.description: The holder, after losing it: their registration is held until an ID of their own is on record.

contestBy.description: They did not get it, and may still make an appointment — until when.

choices.description:
THE DAYS THERE ARE TO CHOOSE FROM, while this person may make or move an appointment: the company's visiting
days in the next three weeks, without the dates it is closed — and, where it counts visitors by the hour, the
hours of each with the places still free. Absent where it has set no visiting days: then any day may be asked.

sent.description: Their photographs have been sent to staff.

dataUrl.description: A downscaled image as a data URL, the way every photograph reaches this network.

at.description: The hour, `HH:MM` — where the country's company counts its visitors by the hour.

nationalId.description: The number on their own ID card.

sentAt.description: Their photographs have been sent, and when.

face.description: The photographs — media ids, only when one dispute is opened.

card.description: What the number staff read on their card came to.

who.description: Who they are on the network: "Driver: Amos K., with Kilima Logistics", "Shop: Mama Sarah Shop".

since.description: Since when they have had an account.

phoneEnds.description: The last digits of the claimant's phone.

onRecord.description: What the holder sent when they registered, where they sent anything: an ID copy, a portrait. Media ids.

retakeWhy.description: Staff asked for the photographs again.

proposedTo.description: The proposal waiting for a second member of staff — from the photographs, or after an appointment.

proposedByYou.description: The member of staff reading this made the proposal, so cannot be the one to approve it.

sentBackWhy.description: A second member of staff sent it back, and why.

appointmentDate.description: An appointment: the day, and which of the two made it.

appointmentAt.description: The hour of the appointment, where there is one.

appointmentRemindedAt.description: The day-before reminder went to whoever of the two has an account, and when.

appointmentOffDay.description: The appointment is on a day the country's company no longer receives visitors.

place.description:
Where the two people are sent, and when visitors are received there — the country's company's own entry, set
in its own admin. Absent: it has written nothing, and a ticket says to ask.

reference.description: The claimant's reference; the holder has their own.

waiting.description: How many wait on a member of staff.

number.description: The number as read off the card — in the photograph, or in the hand. Only whether it is the disputed one is kept.

reason.description: Why the photographs will not do — written for the person who has to take them again.

what.description: What was checked, and how. Kept: the second member of staff approves on the strength of it.

reason.description: Written for the one who does not get it: they read it.

why.description: Why the second member of staff does not approve it as it stands.

issuer.description: Who issued the licence, or the insurer.

number.description: The licence or policy number: what a reader checks against the issuer's own register.

reportable.description: There is a paper on record behind it that counts, so it can be reported.

pointId.description: A collection point by its public id — exact, and what a merchant's checkout already holds.

address.description: …or where the person actually IS, in their own words: "Bole, Addis Ababa", "12 Biashara St, Kisumu".

country.description: …or an area we already serve, named exactly. `country` narrows either of the two above.

quoteId.description: A price held earlier. Give this OR the four fields below — never both.

buyerMobile.description: Somebody has to be told where to collect it.

contentPhotoRef.description: A photo of the contents — the baseline a damage claim is judged against. Upload it first.

externalOrderId.description: Your own order reference, carried through and returned on every callback.

items.description: What is in the box, and what it is worth. Required when the route crosses a border.

country.description: Two letters, from the country catalogue.

yourName.description: How the person setting it up appears inside it.

reason.description: Why it was refused, in staff's words. Shown so the business can put it right.

missing.description:
WHAT IS STILL MISSING BEFORE IT CAN BE ASKED FOR, in keys a screen turns into sentences. Derived on every read.
`certificate_of_incorporation` · `representative_id`.

state.description: `invited` until they sign in and accept.

you.description: True on the reader's own row.

handle.description: Its public address — only once checked.

you.description: The reader's own place in it.

entityId.description: The expeditor whose book this is.

archivedAt.description: Kept, not deleted: a load sent for them in March still names them.

by.description: The shared operator key's typed name. A named staff session's own name always wins.

entityId.description: The shipper's business on SeeBuyGet, once it linked the contract with the fleet's code. Absent: not here.

linkedBy.description: Which person in the business linked it.

name.description: As the fleet named them — and, once linked, as the business is registered. Box 1 on every order's note.

side.description: Which side ended it, and the person who did.

inviteExpiresAt.description: Whether a link code is outstanding, and until when — never the code.

shipperName.description: Who the fleet carries for — the sender on every order's consignment note until their business links it.

reference.description: Their own contract number. Never a price: the terms are between the two of them.

orderRef.description: The shipper's own order number, where it gave one.

partOf.description: One load of an order that comes in several.

indivisible.description: Goods that are one piece: they cannot go in several loads.

planned.description: P3 — where the accepted plan for its day puts it.

deliveryTiming.description: Delivered: when, on this fleet's own clock, and where that fell against the day and the window asked for.

role.description:
P4 — how the fleet reading this stands to the order: `own` it was ordered from this fleet (whoever carries it now)
· `offered` a partner is offering it to this fleet · `partner` this fleet took it from a partner and carries it.

handOn.description: P4 — offered to partners, with a partner, or on the open board.

fromFleetName.description: P4 — the fleet that handed it on, where that is not the fleet reading this.

postedByName.description: Who in the shipper's business ordered it, and the client an expeditor ordered it for.

driverName.description: On a truck: who drives it and which vehicle.

uploaded.description: Whether this fleet's office uploaded it (and so may withdraw it) rather than the shipper ordering it.

late.description: Its delivery day is over and it has not arrived. Computed on the server's clock, never typed.

workbook.description: The .xlsx file itself, base64. A megabyte of workbook at most.

pickupLabel.description: Where the goods are collected, for every line that does not say otherwise. Both, or neither.

verdict.description:
`ok` it can be (or was) imported · `duplicate` an order with this number is already under the contract, so it is
left alone · `problem` it is not imported, and `problems` says why.

line.description: The line as a person counts it: the header is line 1.

located.description: Whether the delivery address has a point on the map. An order without one is imported, and cannot be planned until it has.

refusal.description: Why the sheet as a whole could not be read. Then there are no rows.

columns.description: Which of the sheet's own headings was read as what, and which were made nothing of.

sheet.description: For a workbook: the sheet that was read — only ever the first — and the names of the ones that were not.

imported.description: Whether anything was created: false for a check, true for an import.

keepOff.description: P5 — keep these orders off these vehicles; put these orders on these vehicles.

deliveryWindow.description: The window in the shipper's own words.

window.description: The window as the plan READ those words ("08:00–12:00", "before 14:00") — what it planned to. Absent: no window, or words it could not read as one.

windowUnread.description: The shipper wrote something about when, and the plan could not read it as a time: it is shown, and was not planned to.

lateMin.description: Minutes after its window closed that the door is reached. Planned all the same, and said.

earlyMin.description: Minutes before its window opens that the goods are handed over: the day had no room to wait.

waitMin.description: Minutes the truck stands at the door before its window opens; `arrive` is then the opening.

km.description: Kilometres from the collection, or from the stop before.

arrive.description: When the goods are handed over at this door, on the clock (HH:MM). An estimate from distance and the day's settings.

siteId.description: The fleet's own site it loads at. Absent: it loads somewhere else — a shipper's yard.

openWaitMin.description: Minutes it stands at the site before it opens; `start` is then the opening.

bayWaitMin.description: Minutes it waits there for a bay, every one taken by another truck.

afterCloseMin.description: Minutes it is still loading after the site has closed. Planned all the same, and said.

emptyKm.description: Empty running to reach the collection: from the depot, or from where the last trip ended.

overMin.description: Minutes its day runs past its shift: waiting for a bay, which is handed out after the day is planned.

siteId.description: The site it starts from and comes back to, and the shift it goes out on where the site has shifts.

minutes.description: Site to site, in minutes; when it leaves, and when it is back.

weightKg.description: Everything it carries in the day, over all its trips.

fullestPct.description: Its fullest trip, as a share of what it carries at once (0–100).

splitInto.description:
For an order heavier than the fleet's largest vehicle that the office MAY split: how many loads of that vehicle
it would make. A suggestion — the office decides, and the shipper is told.

bays.description: How many load at once. Absent: not said — as many as come.

hours.description: Open for loading that day ("06:00–18:00"). Absent: it never closes — or, with `closed`, not at all that day.

drivers.description: Drivers who start from here that day: no more trucks leave it than this.

loadings.description: Trips that load here, of any truck.

bayWaits.description: Loadings that waited for a bay, and the longest wait.

afterClose.description: Loadings still going on after it closes.

orders.description: How many of the orders left near this site the trucks below would carry from here, and what they weigh.

trucks.description: How many more trucks like the fleet's largest the leftover orders would take.

capacityKg.description: What one of those trucks carries.

orders.description: Orders for the day still without a truck when the plan was made, and how many of them it placed.

drivers.description: Drivers the fleet has to send out — on the day's roster, or every active driver where there is none: the plan uses no more trucks than this.

outsideWindow.description: Planned orders that reach their door outside the window their shipper asked for — late, or early. Each is marked.

unreadWindows.description: Orders whose window is in words the plan could not read as a time. They are planned, to the day only.

dayStart.description: When the trucks leave the depot (HH:MM), and the longest a truck's day may be, in hours.

offRoad.description: Off the road for a reason of its own (papers, status): never planned, and said why.

excluded.description: Left out of this plan by the office.

sites.description: The fleet's sites, each with its trucks and drivers. A plan kept from before there were sites has none: it was all the depot.

shifts.description: Each shift at each site: drivers rostered, and needed. A plan kept from before there were shifts has none.

lend.description: Sites short of trucks, and the fleet's own idle trucks elsewhere that would carry what was left there.

rules.description: The rules this plan was made under. Empty when there are none.

roster.description: Who it counted as driving. A plan kept from before there were rosters has none: it counted everybody.

distances.description: What its distances are. A plan kept from before there was a routing server to ask has none: it was an estimate.

timeZone.description: The clock its times are on: the fleet's own time zone when the plan was made. Absent: the fleet had none.

accepted.description: Set on the plan the office accepted for this day. A proposal has none.

sent.description: The orders that went onto the driver, by code.

held.description: The orders of that trip that were refused, and why. They stay in the queue, marked.

plan.description: The plan as it was accepted — a record, not recomputed. Absent: no plan accepted for this day.

leftOut.description: Orders the accepted plan could not place, still waiting: known about, and somebody's to hire for or pin.

newSince.description: Orders for the day that ARRIVED after the plan was accepted: the plan has never seen them.

withdrawnSince.description: Orders in the accepted plan that have since been withdrawn.

name.description: The zone as somebody names it: East Africa Time.

now.description: The time and the day on that clock, at the moment this was asked.

choices.description: The clocks the fleet's country keeps: the ones an office chooses among. One, where there is nothing to choose.

configured.description: Whether this server can reach the adviser at all.

changed.description:
What changed in the asks, in words — worked out by the server from the asks before and after, never taken from
the adviser's own account of itself.

plan.description: The plan under those asks: a proposal, worked out by the solver. Nothing is accepted by asking.

reply.description: What the adviser said. Empty when it could not answer — `failed` then says why.

shiftId.description: The shift of that site they start on: the one the office said, else the site's first. Absent: the site has no shifts.

siteId.description: The site they start from that day: their home site, unless the office said another for the day.

source.description: `roster` — the office said who drives that day · `everyone` — it has not, so a plan counts every active driver.

list.description: Every active driver of the fleet, and whether they drive that day.

setAt.description: When the office last said, and who. Absent when it never has for this day.

drivers.description: How many drivers a plan for the day counts.

shiftId.description: Which shift of that site. Absent: the site's first.

starts.description: Where a driver starts that day, where it is not their home site. Absent: everybody from home.

fleetName.description: Their fleet. Absent for a driver in no fleet, who has no roster.

km.description: Driven, from its odometer readings within the days. Absent where fewer than two readings were given.

daysOut.description: Days a shift was started in it.

daysOffRoad.description: Days it was off the road — a spell (workshop, service, accident) or a breakdown — and not out.

daysIdle.description: Days it could have gone out and did not.

loads.description: Loads delivered from it, their weight, and the kilometres they were carried loaded and run empty to reach them.

runs.description: Runs that left in it, and the weight booked on them.

km.description: Driven, from its odometer readings within the days. Absent where fewer than two readings were given.

daysOut.description: Days a shift was started in it.

daysOffRoad.description: Days it was off the road — a spell (workshop, service, accident) or a breakdown — and not out.

daysIdle.description: Days it could have gone out and did not.

runs.description: Runs that left in it, and the weight booked on them.

km.description: Driven, from its odometer readings within the days. Absent where fewer than two readings were given.

daysOut.description: Days a shift was started in it.

daysOffRoad.description: Days it was off the road — a spell (workshop, service, accident) or a breakdown — and not out.

daysIdle.description: Days it could have gone out and did not.

loads.description: Loads delivered from it, their weight, and the kilometres they were carried loaded and run empty to reach them.

runs.description: Runs that left in it, and the weight booked on them.

days.description: The days counted: from `from` to `to`, or to today where `to` has not come.

loadingBays.description: Absent: not said — as many load at once as come.

main.description: The depot the fleet signed up with.

vehicles.description: How many of the fleet's vehicles, and of its active drivers, work from here.

name.description: Its plate, or the driver's name.

loadingBays.description: How many trucks load there at once. `null` here: not counted — as many as come.

hours.description: Open for loading, day by day ({ mon: { open: '06:00', close: '18:00' }, sun: null }). `null` here: it never closes.

shifts.description: The whole list of shifts, replacing what was there.

untilDay.description: The last day off the road. Absent: until it is put back by hand.

newMeter.description: The office recorded a new meter: this reading starts again from what it shows.

doubtful.description: Why the reading is doubtful, in words. Absent: nothing odd about it.

hasPhoto.description: The photograph, served by the upkeep routes to the vehicle's owner (GET vehicles/:id/defects/:defectId/photo).

from.description: What the count runs from: the last service, or (none yet) when the vehicle was registered — and that day.

line.description: The state in words, as notices and the vehicle's row say it.

id.description: The order's id, or the run booking's.

label.description: What the office calls it: the order's code, or what the booking said it was.

shipperTold.description: Its shipper is somebody here, and was told. The fleet's own loads tell nobody.

loads.description: What moved: order codes, and what run bookings said they were.

by.description: Who recorded it: the driver who took them over, or the office.

driverDid.description: The driver on a shift in it then, if anybody was.

locationFrom.description: Where the position came from: the phone as it was reported, or the shift's last known.

held.description: Today's planned orders that were waiting for it, held: their codes.

stillAboard.description: DERIVED on read: what of it is still with the driver it broke down under — what a handover would move.

handovers.description: Its loads, taken over by other vehicles of the fleet.

grounded.description: Grounded before grounding had a way back: "back on the road" returns it.

spells.description: Spells now or to come, soonest first; ended ones are history and not listed.

odometer.description: The latest odometer reading. Absent: none yet.

readings.description: The last few readings, newest first.

defects.description: Defects still open, safety-critical first; and the last few decided.

service.description: The next service: when it is due, and how it stands.

services.description: What was done to it, newest first.

breakdowns.description: Broken down: the open one, and those resolved in the last month, newest first.

lastCheckBy.description: The last daily check: who, when, and what it found.

today.description: Today on the owner's clock (the fleet's): what every day on this sheet is judged by — not the reader's device.

usable.description: Can it start a shift now, and if not, every reason — its papers, and whatever else keeps it off the road.

inUse.description: A driver is on a shift in it right now: a spell starting today leaves that shift running, and stops the next.

newMeter.description: A new meter: this reading may be lower than the last, and starts again from here.

driverName.description: Who is with it: the one whose pass hands the loads over.

pass.description: The six digits under "Show my badge" on the other driver's phone — or the whole pass.

safety.description: A problem with it keeps the vehicle off the road until the office has it fixed, or says it is safe as it is.

checkedTodayBy.description: Checked today already (by anybody): who, and when.

required.description: The fleet asks for a check before a shift: none today, and the shift does not start.

alreadyOpen.description: Problems already reported and still open: not reported twice.

serviceOverdue.description: What a service overdue does: only warns (the default), or takes the vehicle off the road until one is recorded.

requireDailyCheck.description: A driver checks the vehicle before a shift, or the shift does not start. Off unless the fleet turns it on.

side.description: Which side ended it: the fleet that offers, or the partner.

mayPassOn.description: Whether the partner may pass this fleet's orders on to a fleet of its own. The offering fleet's switch.

done.description: The orders it was done for, by code.

refused.description: The ones it could not be done for, each with why.

to.description: For an offer: the partner fleets it went to, by name. Empty for a release to the board.

why.description: Why the plan was made on estimates instead, in the words the plan itself carried.

places.description: How many places the plan had.

host.description: The host of the address that is set. Never the address itself.

invalid.description: Something is set, and it is not a web address: no plan can use it.

maxPoints.description: The most places one request carries; a day with more is planned on estimates.

code.description: The provider's own code for the failure, for looking up. A code only: its words may name an address.

again.description: It could not be handed over, and it is KEPT to be tried again. Absent on one that failed and will not be.

what.description: Which email it was, by its name — never who it was for.

host.description: The host of the provider's sending address. Never the address itself, and never the token.

problem.description: A token is set and the provider is not used, and this is why.

bounces.description: The provider's bounce notices: whether they are listened for, and what became of the ones that came.

sends.description: An email leaves this server. `false`: it is kept here instead, and reaches nobody.

tokenSet.description: A provider's token is set. Set while `sends` is false, it is a token nothing on this server uses.

from.description: Who an email says it is from.

fromIsPlaceholder.description:
That address is on a domain set aside for examples — the one this server starts with is — which nobody owns, so
no provider can verify it or will send for it.

written.description: Emails written since this server started, and how many of those could not be handed over.

reserved.description:
Emails NOT handed to the provider since this server started because their address cannot exist: it is on a
domain reserved for examples and tests. Nought while nothing is sent — the outbox keeps those like any other.

bounced.description:
Emails NOT handed to the provider since this server started because email to their address came back: writing
to it again would only bounce again. A code still goes — it is how such an address proves itself.

waiting.description:
Emails that could not be handed over and are being tried again: how many wait NOW, and since when the oldest.
They wait in memory — an address and a link's key are not written to disk to wait — so a restart forgets them.

sentLater.description: Since this server started: handed over on a later try · given up on (turned down, or no longer worth sending).

sends.description: A push leaves this server. `false`: it is kept here instead, and no phone is woken.

devices.description: Devices that have turned notifications on, and how many people they belong to.

handed.description: Pushes handed to a device since this server started, and how many of those failed.

code.description: The provider's own number for the failure, for looking up. A number only: its words may name a phone.

credential.description: Which credential would be used. Absent: none is set.

sender.description: Who a text would be from: a Messaging Service, or a number or sender name. Absent: none is set.

problem.description: Something of the provider's is set and it is not used, and this is why.

sends.description: A text leaves this server for the provider. `false`: it is kept here instead, and no phone receives one.

standIn.description: The texts go to a stand-in on this machine, not to the provider: a sandbox being driven.

countries.description: The countries a code is texted to — the ones that are switched on — each as its code and dial code ("KE +254"). Empty: none.

written.description: Texts written since this server started · of those, not handed over.

fenced.description: Codes NOT texted since this server started because the number's country is not switched on.

sandbox.description:
This is a sandbox, where mail, push and texts are MEANT to be kept and not sent. Off a sandbox the same state is
people who are never told.

since.description: When this server started. "Last asked" is since then: it is kept in memory, and a restart forgets it.

km.description: By road between the two places, as the server has it.

noRoad.description: It answered, and knows no road between them.

apartKm.description: How far apart the two places are in a straight line.

near.description: Whose depot the two places are near.

ms.description: How long it took to answer.

number.description: The note's number, and where the goods went from and to. Only while the link opens it.

opensLeft.description: How many more times it can be opened.

documentUntil.description: Until when the document itself is kept: after that nobody can be given another copy.

sentTo.description: The address it was emailed to, masked. Absent on a link somebody made to pass on themselves.

madeBy.description: Who made it, where a person did and the sign-in names one: in a company, which of its people.

cancelledBy.description: Who cancelled it, where a person did and the sign-in names one.

cancelledWhy.description: Why, when nobody cancelled it by hand.

opened.description: How many times the file was taken with it, and when last.

insurer.description: The insurer's name, as the store wrote it.
Where it was emailed the moment it was made, where the store names an insurer.

notes.description: Notes the receiver added after handover.

links.description: How many links to it are working, and how often the file was taken with one.

shipmentId.description: The shipment's own identity in the network: the same from the moment it was made.

declaredValue.description: What the goods were said to be worth when the parcel was made. Recorded, whether or not anything covers it.

through.description: store — a store's order · counter — handed in at a shop · app — sent from somebody's phone.

promise.description: ours — a company of the network answers · theirs — the carrier's promise · none — nobody's.

coverLimit.description: What that company pays from its own books at most. Zero where it has stated no cover: it pays nothing itself.

heldBy.description: In whose hands it was at that moment, where it was in anybody's.

shop.description: The shop that reported it, when it was reported at a counter.

reason.description: In the words of whoever reported it.

parcelWas.description: Where the parcel was when it was reported: still on a shelf, or already handed over.

by.description: Who wrote it: the receiver, whose goods they are, and who is the one to open the parcel.

sha256.description: SHA-256 over this note, keys sorted, without this field. The report's own fingerprint is untouched by it.

insurer.description: Beside the body, not in it: the fingerprint covers what the report SAYS, and where a copy went is not part of that.

notes.description: What the receiver found after handover, oldest first — beside the body, each with a fingerprint of its own.

sha256.description: SHA-256 over the body, keys sorted. Two copies with the same fingerprint say the same thing.

photoRefs.description: Up to four of their own photographs of what they found.

notes.description: Notes the receiver added after handover — in the file the link opens.
